getting_started.title: Getting started
getting_started.summary: What timebanking is, how to join, and how to find your way around.

what_is_timebanking.title: What is timebanking?
what_is_timebanking.summary: Timebanking lets people help each other using time instead of money. One hour of help earns one time credit.
what_is_timebanking.body:
Timebanking is a way for people in a community to help each other using time instead of money.

When you spend an hour helping another member, you earn one **time credit**. A time credit is a record of one hour. You can then spend your credits to get help from someone else.

## Everyone's time is equal

An hour is an hour, whatever the task. An hour of gardening, an hour of language practice and an hour of computer help are each worth one time credit. Nobody's time is worth more than anyone else's.

## What people exchange

Members offer and ask for all kinds of everyday help, for example:

- a lift to the shops
- help with a form or a phone
- a friendly chat or a walk
- small jobs around the home or garden
- teaching a skill, such as cooking or music

You do not need special qualifications. Everyone has something to offer.

## Who looks after your community

Each community has its own team. **Coordinators** (sometimes called **brokers**) help members connect and keep exchanges safe. **Administrators** look after the community and its settings. If you are unsure about anything, you can ask them.

To read more, open the [Timebanking Guide](/timebanking-guide).

how_time_credits_work.title: How do time credits work?
how_time_credits_work.summary: You earn time credits by giving help and spend them on getting help. Your balance is kept in your wallet.
how_time_credits_work.body:
Time credits move from one member to another when help is given.

1. You and another member agree what help is needed, and when.
2. The help takes place.
3. The member who received the help pays the member who gave it, in time credits. One hour of help is one time credit.

Depending on how your community works, the credits are sent from the wallet, or they move when both members confirm the exchange is complete.

## Your balance

Your balance shows how many credits you have. You can see it in your [Wallet](/wallet). It also appears in hours next to **Wallet** in the menu under your name.

## Things to know

- Time credits are a record of time. They are not money.
- Some communities give new members a few credits to start with. Others start everyone at zero.
- You do not need any credits to offer help. Helping others is how most members earn them.

For step-by-step help with sending credits and reading your history, see the **Wallet** section of this Help Centre.

joining_your_community.title: How do I join?
joining_your_community.summary: Create an account with your name, email address and a password. Some communities also ask for an invite code.
joining_your_community.body:
You join by creating an account on your community's website. Open [Create your account](/register).

On a computer you see one form. On a phone the same form is split into four short steps: **Community**, **Details**, **Account** and **Terms**.

1. If you are asked, choose your **Community**.
2. Choose a **Profile Type**: **Individual**, or **Organisation** if you are joining for a group or charity.
3. Enter your **First Name**, **Last Name**, **Location** and **Phone Number**.
4. Enter your **Email** and choose a **Password**. Type it again in **Confirm Password**.
5. If your community gave you an invite code, enter it in **Invite Code**.
6. Read and accept the terms. Ticking this box also confirms that you are 18 or older.
7. Press **Create Account**.

## About your details

- Your phone number must start with + and your country code. Only your community's administrators can see it.
- For **Location**, your town or city is enough. Other members can see what you type here, so do not enter your home address.
- Your password must be at least 12 characters long. A phrase of three or four words is easy to remember and hard to guess.

## If you cannot sign up

Some communities only accept people with an invite code, keep a waiting list, or are not taking new members right now. The sign-up page tells you if this applies. You can [contact the community](/contact) to ask about joining.

email_confirmation_and_approval.title: Confirming your email and waiting for approval
email_confirmation_and_approval.summary: After you sign up, confirm your email address. In many communities a coordinator also approves each new member.
email_confirmation_and_approval.body:
After you create your account, we send you an email with a link. Open the email and press the link to confirm your email address. You cannot sign in until you have done this.

> Cannot find the email? Look in your junk or spam folder. To get a new link, go to the sign-in page, try to sign in, and press **Resend verification email**.

## Approval by a coordinator

In many communities, a coordinator checks each new account before it can be used. If this applies, you see **Awaiting admin approval** after confirming your email. You get an email once your account is approved.

Until then, if you try to sign in, you see **You're registered and waiting for approval**.

## Other checks your community may use

- **Waiting list**: some communities add new members to a waiting list, and email you when a place opens.
- **Identity check**: some communities ask you to verify your identity before your account is approved. If this is still to do, the sign-in page shows **Continue verification**.

If you have waited a while and heard nothing, [contact the community](/contact).

first_time_setup.title: Setting up your profile for the first time
first_time_setup.summary: The first time you sign in, a short guided setup helps you add a photo, a few words about you, and your skills.
first_time_setup.body:
The first time you sign in, you may see a short guided setup called **Get Started**. It helps other members get to know you.

1. **Welcome**: press **Let's Get Started**.
2. **Profile**: add a photo and write a few words in **About you**. Many communities ask for both before you can continue.
3. **Interests**: choose the kinds of help that interest you. You can skip this step.
4. **Skills**: under **I can offer**, choose what you could help with. Under **I need help with**, choose what you would like help with. The platform creates simple listings for you from these choices.
5. **Safeguarding**: if your community uses this step, you can tell coordinators that you would like extra support. See **What are safeguarding preferences?** in the **Privacy and safety** section.
6. **Confirm**: check the summary under **Review Your Setup**, then press **Complete Setup**.

When you finish, you are taken to your dashboard.

> In some communities you must finish this setup before you can use the rest of the site. You can change your photo and your introduction later in **Settings**.

finding_your_way_around.title: Finding your way around
finding_your_way_around.summary: The menu at the top of the screen, or at the bottom on a phone, takes you to every part of your community.
finding_your_way_around.body:
The menu only shows the parts of the site your community uses. So what you see may be a little different from what other communities see.

## On a computer

Along the top of the screen you will usually find:

- **Feed**: news and posts from your community
- **Explore**: a place to discover what is going on, if your community uses it
- **Timebanking**: your **Listings**, **Exchanges** and **Wallet**
- **Messages**: private conversations with other members
- **Community**: your **Dashboard**, **Members**, **Events**, **Groups** and more

On the right is the bell for your notifications, and a button with your name or photo. Press it for **My Profile**, **Wallet**, **Settings**, **Get the app** and **Log Out**.

## On a phone

A bar along the bottom of the screen has **Feed**, **Listings**, **Create**, **Messages** and **Menu**. Press **Menu** to see everything else, including **Settings**, **Help Center** and **Log Out**.

## Your dashboard

Your [Dashboard](/dashboard) gives you a summary: your balance, your listings, your messages and anything that needs your attention.

> Looking for something? Press **Search** at the top of the screen, if your community uses it.

using_on_your_phone.title: Can I use it on my phone?
using_on_your_phone.summary: Yes. Use your phone's web browser, add the site to your home screen, or try the Android app.
using_on_your_phone.body:
Yes. There are three ways, and you can choose the one that suits you. For step-by-step help for your device, open [Get the app](/install-app).

## 1. Your phone's web browser

Open the website in your phone's browser and sign in. Every page and every feature works, and you always have the newest version. This is the most stable way to use it on a phone.

## 2. Add it to your home screen

You can save the website to your home screen, so it opens from its own icon like an app. This works on Android phones using Chrome, and on Windows computers using Chrome or Edge.

On iPhone and iPad, saving it as an icon does not work reliably yet. The website itself works normally in Safari.

## 3. The Android app

There is an app for Android phones on Google Play. It works on Android 7.0 or later. It is an early release that is still being developed, so some things may not work quite right yet. When you first open it, choose your community from the list.

An app for iPhone and iPad is not available yet.

> Not sure which to choose? Use your phone's web browser.

accessible_version.title: Is there a simpler, more accessible version?
accessible_version.summary: Yes. A simpler, highly accessible version of the site is available. It opens in a new tab.
accessible_version.body:
Yes. Your community also has a simpler, highly accessible version of the site. It uses plain, clear pages, and it is designed to work well with screen readers, keyboards and screen magnifiers.

It is the same community, with the same members. You sign in with the same email address and password.

## How to open it

- On a computer, press **WCAG 2.2 AA Version** in the thin bar at the very top of the screen. If you cannot see the bar, scroll back to the top of the page.
- On a phone, press **Menu**, then press **WCAG 2.2 AA Version** near the bottom.

It opens in a new tab. WCAG 2.2 AA is the name of an international standard for accessible websites.

## Making the main site easier to use

You can also change how the main site looks. Open [Settings](/settings), stay on the **Profile** tab, and scroll down to **Appearance Preferences**. There you can turn on **Large Text**, **High Contrast**, **Reduced Motion** or **Simplified Layout**. See **Changing language, dark mode and text size**.

language_and_appearance.title: Changing language, dark mode and text size
language_and_appearance.summary: Choose your language, switch between light and dark mode, and make text larger or clearer.
language_and_appearance.body:
## Language

On a computer, press the language button in the thin bar at the top of the screen. It shows a short code, such as EN. On a phone, press **Menu** and use the language button near the bottom.

You can also open [Settings](/settings), stay on the **Profile** tab, and use **Language Preference**.

Your choice is saved to your account, so it stays the same when you sign in on another device. The languages you can choose depend on your community.

## Light and dark mode

Open the menu under your name and press **Dark Mode** or **Light Mode**.

Or, in **Settings** on the **Profile** tab, find **Theme** and choose **Light**, **Dark** or **System**. **System** follows the setting on your device.

## Text size and other display options

In **Settings**, on the **Profile** tab, scroll down to **Appearance Preferences**. There you can:

- change the **Font Size**
- choose an **Accent Color** for buttons and links
- change the **Layout Density**, which is how much space there is between things
- turn on **Large Text**, **High Contrast**, **Reduced Motion** or **Simplified Layout**

**Reduced Motion** cuts down on animation. **Simplified Layout** removes decorative effects such as shadows and blur.

account_profile.title: Your account and profile
account_profile.summary: Edit your profile, see what other members can see, and add your skills.

editing_your_profile.title: How do I edit my profile?
editing_your_profile.summary: Change your photo, name, introduction and location on the Profile tab in Settings.
editing_your_profile.body:
You edit your profile in **Settings**.

1. Open [Settings](/settings). Or open [your profile](/profile) and press **Edit Profile**.
2. Stay on the **Profile** tab.
3. Change what you need under **Profile Information**.
4. Press **Save Changes**.

## What you can change

- **Profile Photo**: press your photo, then choose **Take photo** or **Choose from library**. Use a JPG, PNG, GIF or WebP picture, up to 5MB.
- **First Name** and **Last Name**.
- **Tagline**: one short line about you.
- **Bio**: a few sentences about who you are and what you enjoy.
- **Location**: your town or city.
- **Phone Number**: only your community's administrators can see this.
- **Profile Type**: **Individual** or **Organisation**. An organisation account shows its **Organisation Name** instead of a person's name.
- **Date of Birth**: you only need this if you want to verify your identity. If you enter it, it must show you are 18 or over.

> If your identity has been verified, your name and date of birth are locked. This keeps them matching your ID.

A friendly photo and a short bio help other members feel comfortable getting in touch.

what_other_members_see.title: What can other members see about me?
what_other_members_see.summary: Other members see your first name, photo, introduction and rough location. Your email and phone number stay private.
what_other_members_see.body:
Your profile helps members decide who to exchange with. This is what other members can see.

## What members can see

- your first name (your last name is hidden from other members)
- your profile photo, tagline and bio
- the location you typed, such as your town
- your skills and the times you are usually available, if you added them
- how many hours you have given and received, your rating and your badges
- whether you have been online recently

If your profile type is **Organisation**, members see the organisation's name.

## What members cannot see

- your email address
- your phone number
- your date of birth
- your time credit balance
- your exact position on a map: other members only see a rough area, to within about 1 km

Your community's coordinators and administrators can see more, including your full name and contact details. They need this to support members and keep people safe.

You can also choose who can see your profile at all. See **Who can see my profile?** in the **Privacy and safety** section.

skills_and_availability.title: Adding your skills and availability
skills_and_availability.summary: List what you can do and show the times you are usually free, so the right members can find you.
skills_and_availability.body:
Skills and availability help the right people find you.

## Add your skills

1. Open [Settings](/settings) and choose the **Skills** tab.
2. Under **Your Skills**, press **Add Skill**.
3. In the **Add a Skill** window, type a skill, for example "gardening".
4. Choose one of the suggestions. If nothing matches, you can add your own wording instead.
5. If you like, choose a **Category (optional)** and a **Proficiency Level**: **Beginner**, **Intermediate**, **Advanced** or **Expert**.
6. Press **Add Skill**.

To remove a skill, press the remove button next to it. Other members can endorse your skills, which shows that others value them.

## Show when you are free

1. In [Settings](/settings), choose the **Availability** tab.
2. Press the time slots when you are usually available.
3. Press **Save**.

Your availability is shown on your profile. It is only a guide. You always agree the actual time with the other member.

To see what skills other members offer, open the [Skills](/skills) page.

why_you_are_not_listed.title: Why can't other members find me?
why_you_are_not_listed.summary: The member directory only lists people who have finished their profile and are happy to be found.
why_you_are_not_listed.body:
Not every member appears in the [Members](/members) directory. Your community decides what a profile needs before it is listed. Usually this means:

- you have finished setting up your profile
- you have added a profile photo
- you have written a short introduction
- your privacy settings let people find you

If some members are not listed, the Members page shows a note about it. Press **Why?** to see what your community asks for, then press **Check whether you are listed**.

## Check your privacy settings

1. Open [Settings](/settings) and choose the **Privacy** tab.
2. Look at **Who can see your profile**. If it is set to **Connections Only - Your connections**, only your connections can see you.
3. Look at **Search Engine Indexing**. If it is turned off, you are also left out of the member directory and member search inside your community, not only outside search engines.
4. Press **Save Privacy Settings**.

> Some communities hide a profile from other members until it has a photo and a bio. Adding both is often the quickest fix.

identity_verification.title: How do I get the ID Verified badge?
identity_verification.summary: Verify your identity with a photo ID and a selfie, and an ID Verified badge appears on your profile.
identity_verification.body:
If your community offers it, you can verify your identity. When it is done, an **ID Verified** badge appears on your profile. It is optional, unless your community asks for it when you join.

## What you need

- a valid government-issued photo ID
- a device with a camera
- about 2 to 5 minutes

## How to do it

1. Press **Verify Your Identity** at the top of the screen. On a phone, press **Menu** first. Or open [Verify your identity](/verify-identity-optional).
2. Enter your **Date of Birth** and press **Continue**. It must match your ID.
3. If your community charges a fee, you see the amount. It is a one-time fee. Press **Pay** to continue.
4. Press **Start Verification**. Follow the steps to take a photo of your ID and a selfie.
5. Wait for the result. The page updates by itself.

## After verification

Your name and date of birth are then locked, so they always match your ID.

If verification is unsuccessful, check that your photo of your ID is clear and well lit, and that your name and date of birth match your profile. Then press **Try Again**.

> The check is carried out by an outside verification service. The badge shows that an ID was checked. It does not guarantee that someone is safe, so keep following the usual safety advice.

security_signin.title: Signing in and security
security_signin.summary: Sign in, reset a forgotten password, and keep your account secure.

signing_in.title: How do I sign in?
signing_in.summary: Sign in with your email address and password, or with a passkey or another account if your community allows it.
signing_in.body:
1. Open [Sign in](/login).
2. If you are asked, choose your **Community**.
3. Enter your **Email** and **Password**. To check what you typed, press the eye button in the password box.
4. Press **Sign In**.

## Other ways to sign in

- **Passkey**: if your community offers passkeys and you have set one up, press **Sign in with a passkey**.
- **Google, Apple or Facebook**: if your community allows it, you see buttons such as **Continue with Google**. You can connect or disconnect these accounts in [Settings](/settings), on the **Connected** tab. You cannot disconnect your only way of signing in.

## If you use two-step verification

After your password, you are asked for the six-digit code from your authenticator app. Enter it in **Authentication Code** and press **Verify**. You can tick the box to trust the device for a number of days, so you are not asked every time.

## Signing out

Open the menu under your name and press **Log Out**. On a phone, press **Menu**, then **Log Out**. Always sign out when you use a shared or public computer.

> After too many wrong attempts, signing in is paused for a short time. Wait, then try again, or reset your password.

forgotten_password.title: I forgot my password
forgotten_password.summary: Ask for a reset link by email, then choose a new password. The link works for one hour.
forgotten_password.body:
You can choose a new password using a link we email to you.

1. On the [sign-in page](/login), press **Forgot password?**. Or open [Reset your password](/password/forgot).
2. Enter your **Email address**.
3. Press **Send reset instructions**.
4. Open the email and press the link.
5. Enter your **New Password**, then type it again to confirm it.
6. Press **Reset Password**.
7. Sign in with your new password.

## Good to know

- The link works for one hour. If it has expired, press **Request new link**.
- For your security, the page always says an email has been sent, even if that address is not registered. If nothing arrives, check your junk or spam folder, and check you used the email address you signed up with.
- Your new password must be at least 12 characters long. It cannot be one of your recent passwords.
- After a reset, you are signed out on all your devices. Sign in again with your new password.

> If you ask for several links in a short time, you may need to wait up to an hour before you can ask again.

changing_password.title: How do I change my password?
changing_password.summary: Change your password on the Security tab in Settings. You need your current password.
changing_password.body:
1. Open [Settings](/settings) and choose the **Security** tab.
2. Press **Change Password**.
3. Enter your **Current Password**.
4. Enter your **New Password**, then type it again in **Confirm New Password**.
5. Press **Change Password**.

## Good to know

- Your new password must be at least 12 characters long.
- You cannot reuse one of your recent passwords.
- After the change, your account is signed out on your other devices, such as another phone or computer. You may need to sign in again on this device too.
- You get a notification to tell you that your password was changed. If you did not change it, reset your password straight away and contact your community.

> A phrase of three or four ordinary words is easier to remember, and harder to guess, than one word with symbols.

changing_email.title: Can I change my email address?
changing_email.summary: You cannot change your email address yourself. Your community's administrators can change it for you.
changing_email.body:
At the moment you cannot change the email address on your account yourself. This protects your account, because changing the email address is a common way for someone else to take over an account.

Your community's administrators can change it for you. [Contact your community](/contact) and tell them:

- your name
- the email address you use now
- the new email address you want to use

They may ask you some questions to check that the request really comes from you.

## If you have lost access to your old email

You can still sign in with your password. But you cannot use **Forgot password?** until your email address is updated, so contact your community as soon as you can.

> Never share your password, even with someone who says they are from your community. Coordinators and administrators do not need your password to help you.

two_step_verification.title: Turning on two-step verification
two_step_verification.summary: Add a code from an app on your phone to your sign-in, so a stolen password is not enough to get in.
two_step_verification.body:
Two-step verification, also called two-factor authentication, adds a second check when you sign in. After your password, you enter a six-digit code from an app on your phone. The code changes every 30 seconds. Even if someone learns your password, they cannot sign in without your phone.

## Before you start

Install a free authenticator app on your phone, such as **Google Authenticator**, **Microsoft Authenticator** or **Authy**.

## Turn it on

1. Open [Settings](/settings) and choose the **Security** tab.
2. Next to **Two-Factor Authentication**, press **Enable**.
3. Open your authenticator app and scan the QR code on the screen. If you cannot scan it, type the **Manual entry key** into the app instead.
4. Type the six-digit code from the app into **Verification Code**.
5. Press **Verify & Enable**.
6. You now see **Your Backup Codes**. Save them somewhere safe, for example written on paper at home. Then press **I've Saved My Codes**.

## Backup codes

Each backup code works once. If you lose your phone, press **Use backup code instead** when you sign in, and enter one of them. You can make a new set of codes under **Recovery codes** on the **Security** tab.

## Turning it off

Press **Disable**, enter your password, then press **Disable 2FA**. Some accounts, such as administrator accounts, must keep it turned on.

> Lost your phone and your backup codes? Contact your community's coordinator to get back into your account.

passkeys.title: Signing in with a passkey
passkeys.summary: Use your fingerprint, your face or your device screen lock to sign in, instead of typing a password.
passkeys.body:
A passkey lets you sign in with your fingerprint, your face or your device's screen lock, instead of typing a password. A passkey only works on your community's real website, which helps protect you from fake sites.

## Set up a passkey

1. Sign in with your password as usual.
2. Open [Settings](/settings) and choose the **Security** tab.
3. Find **Passkey Login** and press **Create a passkey**.
4. Confirm it is you, with your password or a code, then press **Confirm**.
5. Follow the steps your device shows, for example touch the fingerprint reader or use Windows Hello.

Each device needs its own passkey, unless your passkey service copies them for you. For example, iCloud Keychain copies passkeys between Apple devices. To add another device, open this page on that device and press **Add another passkey**.

## Sign in with a passkey

On the sign-in page, press **Sign in with a passkey**, then follow the steps on your device.

## Manage your passkeys

On the **Security** tab you can **Rename passkey**, **Remove passkey** or **Remove All Passkeys**. After a change, you may need to sign in again on your other devices.

> If your passkey does not appear when you sign in, sign in with your password instead. Then remove the old passkey and create a new one.

someone_got_into_account.title: What if someone else has got into my account?
someone_got_into_account.summary: Change your password straight away, which signs your account out everywhere. Then check your security settings.
someone_got_into_account.body:
If you think someone else has used your account, act quickly.

1. **Change your password.** Open [Settings](/settings), choose the **Security** tab and press **Change Password**. This signs your account out on your other devices.
2. If you cannot sign in, use [Forgot password?](/password/forgot) to set a new password. This also signs your account out everywhere.
3. **Look at Active Sessions** on the **Security** tab. It lists the browsers and devices that have been signed in, and when each was last used.
4. **Turn on two-step verification**, if your community offers it. See **Turning on two-step verification**.
5. **Check your passkeys**, if you have any. Remove any you do not recognise.
6. If you already use two-step verification, press **Forget all trusted devices**, so every device must enter a code again.
7. **Tell your community.** [Contact them](/contact), so a coordinator can check for anything unusual, such as messages or time credits sent from your account.

## Protect your account in future

- Use a password that you do not use anywhere else.
- Never share your password or your codes with anyone.
- Sign out when you use a shared computer.
- Be careful with emails that ask you to sign in. Check the website address before you type your password.

privacy_safety.title: Privacy and safety
privacy_safety.summary: Keep your details private, choose who sees your profile, block or report problems, and stay safe.

contact_details_private.title: Do other members see my phone number or email?
contact_details_private.summary: No. Other members never see your phone number or email address. Use private messages to arrange exchanges.
contact_details_private.body:
No. Other members cannot see your email address or your phone number. Your phone number is only visible to your community's administrators, so they can contact you if they need to.

## Talk through private messages

You can talk to other members in [Messages](/messages), the private messaging built into the site. You do not need to share a phone number, an email address, WhatsApp or a social media account to arrange an exchange.

Keeping your conversations in **Messages** helps you:

- keep your contact details private
- keep a record of what you agreed
- get help from your community if something goes wrong

> Be careful if someone you have not met asks you to move to a phone call, text messages or another app straight away. It is fine to say no and stay in **Messages**.

## If you decide to share your details

Some members choose to swap phone numbers once they know and trust each other. That is up to you. Only share what you are comfortable with. Never share passwords, bank details or identity documents.

who_can_see_profile.title: Who can see my profile?
who_can_see_profile.summary: Choose whether your profile can be seen by anyone, by community members only, or by your connections only.
who_can_see_profile.body:
You choose who can see your profile in your privacy settings.

1. Open [Settings](/settings) and choose the **Privacy** tab.
2. Under **Profile Visibility**, open **Who can see your profile**.
3. Choose one of the options below.
4. Press **Save Privacy Settings**.

The options are:

- **Public - Anyone can view**
- **Members Only - Community members**: only people who are signed in
- **Connections Only - Your connections**: only members you are connected with

## Search Engine Indexing

The **Search Engine Indexing** switch controls whether search engines, such as Google, may list your profile. Turning it off also takes you out of the member directory, member search and @mentions inside your community.

## Partner communities

If your community is linked with partner communities, press **Federation Settings** on the same tab. There you can choose what members of those communities can see.

Your community's administrators can still see your account details, so they can support you.

blocking_members.title: How do I block someone?
blocking_members.summary: Blocking stops a member from seeing your profile, messaging you or interacting with your content.
blocking_members.body:
If a member is bothering you, you can block them.

1. Open the member's profile.
2. Press the **More options** button (three dots).
3. Press **Block User**.
4. Read the message, then press **Block User** again to confirm.

You can also block someone from the three-dot menu on one of their posts in the feed.

## What blocking does

- They cannot see your profile.
- They cannot send you messages.
- They cannot interact with your content.
- Any connection between you is removed.

## Unblocking someone

1. Open [Settings](/settings), choose the **Privacy** tab and press **Blocked Users**. Or go straight to [Blocked Users](/settings/blocked).
2. Press **Unblock** next to the person.
3. Confirm that you want to unblock them.

They can then see your profile and message you again. You are not reconnected automatically.

> Blocking protects you, but it does not tell your community about a problem. If someone has behaved badly or made you feel unsafe, also tell a coordinator.

reporting_content.title: How do I report a listing or a post?
reporting_content.summary: Press Report listing on a listing, or Report Post on a feed post. Your community reviews reports.
reporting_content.body:
If you see something that breaks the rules, looks like a scam or worries you, report it.

## Report a listing

1. Open the listing.
2. Press **Report listing**.
3. Choose a reason, for example **Safety concern** or **Spam or scam**.
4. If you want to, add more in **Additional details**.
5. Press **Submit Report**.

## Report a post in the feed

1. Press the three-dot menu on the post.
2. Press **Report Post**.
3. Describe the problem in **Reason**.
4. Press **Submit Report**.

Reports go to your community's moderators, who review them.

## Worried about a person?

If a member's behaviour worries you, or you feel unsafe, [contact your community](/contact) and explain what happened. You can also block the member.

> If anyone is in immediate danger, contact your local emergency services first.

safeguarding_preferences.title: What are safeguarding preferences?
safeguarding_preferences.summary: Safeguarding preferences let you ask for extra protection, such as a coordinator checking matches before they go ahead.
safeguarding_preferences.body:
Safeguarding preferences let you ask for extra protection when you use the platform. They are for anyone who would like more support, for example if you consider yourself a vulnerable adult.

You can choose them during your first-time setup, if your community uses this step. Your community writes the questions.

## What they can switch on

Depending on your answers, one or more of these protections may apply. They are shown as labels next to each preference:

- **Broker review**: a coordinator (also called a broker) checks and approves exchanges and matches involving you before they go ahead. This does not let them read your messages.
- **Match approval**: a coordinator approves matches involving you before they are suggested to the other member.
- **Vetted contacts only**: only members your community has confirmed through its own checks can find you and contact you.

Some answers may mean that other members contact you through a coordinator, instead of messaging you directly. A coordinator may also get in touch to talk about how they can help.

## Who can see them

Only your community's coordinators and administrators can see your safeguarding preferences. Other members cannot, and they never appear on your profile.

## Removing a preference

1. Open [Settings](/settings) and choose the **Safeguarding & support** tab.
2. Find the preference and press **Revoke**.
3. Press **Yes, revoke**.

Your coordinators are told about the change.

> Would you like extra support but did not choose it during setup? Contact your community coordinator.

coordinator_message_review.title: Can a coordinator read my messages?
coordinator_message_review.summary: Some conversations may be reviewed by a coordinator for safeguarding. You see a notice when this can happen.
coordinator_message_review.body:
Your messages are private between you and the other member. In some situations, a coordinator may review a conversation to keep people safe.

When this can happen, you see a notice in the conversation. It says that messages may be reviewed by a coordinator for safeguarding, or seen by someone a member trusts to support them.

Choosing your own safeguarding preferences does not, on its own, let coordinators read your messages.

## When you cannot message someone directly

Sometimes you see a notice instead of the message box. This is usually because of the other member's safeguarding preferences.

- **Coordinator arrangement needed**: the member needs a coordinator to arrange contact. Press **Request coordinator help**, and a coordinator will be in touch.
- **Community confirmation needed**: the member only accepts contact from members your community has confirmed. Press **Request review of my vetting** to ask your community to review this. You can also do this in [Settings](/settings), on the **Safeguarding & support** tab, with **Request broker review**.
- **Safeguarding check temporarily unavailable**: press **Check again**. If it keeps happening, ask a coordinator for help.

> Do not upload or send any police check or criminal record document through the platform. Your community arranges any checks outside the platform.

staying_safe.title: Staying safe when you meet someone
staying_safe.summary: Simple habits that help exchanges go well, especially the first time you meet someone.
staying_safe.body:
Most exchanges go smoothly. These habits help keep it that way.

## Before you meet

- Read the member's profile, and their reviews if they have any.
- Keep your conversation in **Messages**, so there is a record of what you agreed.
- Agree clearly what will happen, when, where and for how long.
- For a first meeting, choose a public place if you can, or make sure someone else is nearby.
- Tell a friend or relative where you are going and when you expect to be back.

## During the exchange

- Trust your instincts. If something feels wrong, you can stop and leave.
- You do not have to let anyone into your home if you are not comfortable.
- Do not hand over money, bank cards, passwords or identity documents.

## Afterwards

- If something went wrong or worried you, tell a coordinator. [Contact your community](/contact).
- If you feel unsafe, block the member.

> If anyone is in immediate danger, contact your local emergency services first.

If an activity involves a vulnerable adult, ask your coordinator which rules apply.

adults_only.title: Can people under 18 join?
adults_only.summary: No. The platform is for adults aged 18 and over.
adults_only.body:
No. The platform is for adults aged 18 and over.

When you create an account, you confirm that you are 18 or older.

If an account has a date of birth showing the person is under 18, that account cannot be used. Signing in shows a message that explains why.

You do not have to give your date of birth to join. You only need it if you choose to verify your identity. If you do enter a date of birth, it must show that you are 18 or over.

If you think an account has been refused by mistake, [contact the community](/contact).

> If you are worried that someone under 18 is using the platform, tell your community.

notifications.title: Notifications
notifications.summary: See alerts under the bell, and choose which emails and phone notifications you get.

notification_bell.title: What is the bell at the top of the screen?
notification_bell.summary: The bell shows your notifications, such as new messages and replies. A number shows how many are unread.
notification_bell.body:
The bell at the top of the screen shows your notifications. A number on it tells you how many you have not read yet.

Press the bell to see your latest notifications. Press one to go to the page it is about. Press **View all notifications** to open the full list.

On a phone, you can also press **Menu**. The number next to **Alerts** shows your unread notifications. Press it to open them.

## On the Notifications page

On the [Notifications](/notifications) page you can:

- switch between **All** and **Unread**
- press **Mark all read** to clear the unread count
- delete a notification you no longer need. If you delete one by mistake, press **Undo** straight away.
- press **Settings** to choose which notifications you get

> While you are using the site, some notifications also appear as a small pop-up, for example when a new message arrives.

email_notification_settings.title: Choosing which emails you get
email_notification_settings.summary: Turn email notifications on or off for messages, listings, events, reviews and more.
email_notification_settings.body:
You decide which emails you get.

1. Open [Settings](/settings) and choose the **Notifications** tab.
2. Turn each switch on or off.
3. Press **Save Preferences**.

## What you can choose

The switches you see depend on what your community uses. They include:

- **New Messages**: when someone sends you a message
- **Connection Requests**
- **Event emails**: changes, cancellations and reminders for events
- **Listing Activity**: responses to your listings
- **Credit Transactions**: when time credits move in or out of your wallet
- **New Reviews**
- **Monthly Digest**: a monthly summary of community activity
- **Marketing Emails**: newsletters and community updates

If you have an organisation account, you may also see **Organisation Notifications**.

## Emails you cannot turn off

Some emails are needed to keep your account working, so there is no switch for them. For example, emails that confirm your email address or reset your password.

> Want fewer emails? See **Getting a summary email instead**.

email_digests.title: Getting a summary email instead
email_digests.summary: Choose how often you get summary emails about group activity and suggested matches.
email_digests.body:
A digest is one email that gathers several updates together, instead of sending one email for each thing.

Open [Settings](/settings) and choose the **Notifications** tab. Then use the settings below, and press **Save Preferences** when you are done.

## Activity in your groups and threads

Find **Activity digest frequency** and choose:

- **Off**: no digest emails. This is where it starts.
- **Instant**: an email as things happen
- **Daily**: one email a day
- **Monthly**: one email a month

Direct messages, connection requests and confirmations about time credits are not held back for a digest.

## Suggested matches

If your community uses listings, find **Match Digest Emails**. Under **Digest Frequency**, choose **Daily**, **Fortnightly**, **Monthly** or **Never**.

You can also turn on **Hot Match Alerts**, for very good matches, and **Mutual Match Alerts**, for when someone you matched with also matches with you.

## A monthly summary

Turn on **Monthly Digest** to get a monthly summary of what is happening in your community.

push_notifications.title: Getting notifications on your phone or computer
push_notifications.summary: Turn on push notifications to get alerts on your device, even when the site is not open.
push_notifications.body:
Push notifications are alerts that pop up on your phone or computer, like a text message alert. They can arrive even when the site is not open.

## Turn them on

1. On the device where you want alerts, open [Settings](/settings) and choose the **Notifications** tab.
2. Under **Push Notifications**, turn on **Enable Push Notifications**.
3. When your browser asks, allow notifications for this site.

When it has worked, you see **You are subscribed on this device.** Repeat this on each device you use.

## If it does not work

- If you see **You have blocked notifications**, your browser is set to block them for this site. Change the notification permission for this site in your browser settings, then try again.
- If you see **Your browser does not support push notifications**, try a different browser, or add the site to your home screen. See **Can I use it on my phone?**

## In the Android app

The Android app can send you notifications even when it is closed. Allow notifications when the app asks. See [Get the app](/install-app).

## Turning them off

Turn off **Enable Push Notifications**. You can also block notifications for the site in your browser or phone settings.

your_data.title: Your data and account
your_data.summary: Download your data, make a data request, delete your account, and manage cookies.

download_your_data.title: How do I download my data?
download_your_data.summary: Download a copy of the information your community holds about you, as a file you can keep.
download_your_data.body:
You can download a copy of the information your community holds about you. This includes your profile, the hours you have given and received, your transactions, listings, events and more.

1. Open [Settings](/settings) and choose the **Privacy** tab.
2. Press **Download Your Data**. Or go straight to [Download Your Data](/settings/data-export).
3. Under **Format**, choose the kind of file you want. The choices are explained below.
4. Press **Download my data**.

The two formats are:

- **ZIP archive (human-friendly)**: includes a guide that explains each part. Choose this if you are not sure.
- **JSON (developer-friendly)**: one structured file. It is useful if you want to move your data to another service.

The file is prepared and saved to your device. Your past downloads are listed under **Recent exports**. You can download your data up to 5 times a day.

> The file contains your personal information. Keep it somewhere private, and only share it with people you trust.

data_rights_requests.title: Asking to correct or limit the use of your data
data_rights_requests.summary: Send a request to correct your data, limit how it is used, or object to it being used.
data_rights_requests.body:
You have rights over your personal data. As well as downloading it, you can send your community a request. Open [Settings](/settings), choose the **Privacy** tab and find **Data & Privacy Rights**.

- **Data Rectification**: ask for information about you to be corrected, if it is wrong or incomplete.
- **Restriction of Processing**: ask for your data to be stored, but not actively used.
- **Right to Object**: object to your data being used for a particular purpose, such as marketing.

## Sending a request

1. Press the request you want to make.
2. Read the explanation. It tells you how long a response can take.
3. Press **Submit Request**.

A confirmation email is sent to your email address.

> You can correct most of your details yourself, straight away, on the **Profile** tab in **Settings**. A request is useful for things you cannot change yourself.

deleting_your_account.title: How do I delete my account?
deleting_your_account.summary: You can permanently delete your account from Settings. This cannot be undone.
deleting_your_account.body:
You can delete your account yourself. This is permanent and cannot be undone.

## Before you delete

- If you want to keep a copy of your data, download it first. See **How do I download my data?**
- Any time credits left in your wallet are not paid out or passed to anyone. If you would like them to go to another member, send them before you delete your account.
- Finish or cancel any exchanges you have agreed with other members.

## Delete your account

1. Open [Settings](/settings) and choose the **Security** tab.
2. Under **Account Actions**, press **Delete Account**. You can also find **Delete your account** on the **Privacy** tab.
3. Type the word **DELETE** in the box.
4. Enter your **Current Password**.
5. Press **Delete My Account**.

You are signed out, and an email is sent to confirm that your account has been deleted.

## What happens to your information

Your name, contact details, profile, photo, active listings and preferences are removed or made anonymous. The words of messages you wrote are removed, but the other person keeps an anonymous record of the conversation. Records of past exchanges and time credits are kept without your name, because other members' records depend on them.

cookie_settings.title: Changing your cookie choices
cookie_settings.summary: Choose whether to allow optional cookies, and change your choice at any time.
cookie_settings.body:
Cookies are small files that a website saves in your browser. When you first visit, you see a message called **We use cookies**. You can press:

- **Accept all** to allow all cookies
- **Essential only** to allow only the cookies the site needs to work
- **Manage preferences** to choose for yourself

## The types of cookie

- **Essential**: needed for signing in, security and reporting faults. These are **Always on**.
- **Analytics**: help the community understand how the site is used, such as usage statistics, page timings and recordings of how pages are used. These are optional.
- **Preferences**: remember your choices, such as theme and language. These are optional.

## Change your choice later

- On a computer, press **Cookie Settings** at the bottom of any page.
- On a phone, press **Menu**, open **Legal**, and press **Manage preferences**.

Make your choices, then press **Save preferences**.

For more detail, read the [Cookie Policy](/cookies).

legal_documents.title: Where can I read the terms and privacy policy?
legal_documents.summary: Your community's legal documents, such as the terms and the privacy policy, are all in one place.
legal_documents.body:
You can read your community's legal documents at any time, without signing in:

- [Terms of Service](/terms)
- [Privacy Policy](/privacy)
- [Cookie Policy](/cookies)
- [Accessibility Statement](/accessibility)
- [Community Guidelines](/community-guidelines)
- [Acceptable Use Policy](/acceptable-use)

They are all listed together on the [Legal](/legal) page. On a phone, you can also press **Menu** and open **Legal**.

## When a document changes

If an important document is updated, you may see **Updated legal documents** when you next use the site. Press **Read** to open each document. When you are ready, press **Accept & Continue**. You need to accept the updated documents to keep using the site.

If you do not agree with a change, [contact your community](/contact) before you accept it.

troubleshooting.title: Help and troubleshooting
troubleshooting.summary: What to do when you cannot sign in, emails do not arrive, or something is not working.

cant_sign_in.title: I can't sign in
cant_sign_in.summary: The most common reasons you cannot sign in, and what to do about each one.
cant_sign_in.body:
Find the message or problem you have, then follow the advice.

## Wrong email or password

Check you are using the email address you signed up with, and that Caps Lock is off. Press the eye button to see what you typed. If you still cannot get in, press **Forgot password?** and set a new password.

## Too many attempts

If you see **Too many attempts**, wait a few minutes, then try again.

## Your email is not confirmed

Press **Resend verification email**, then open the link in the new email. Check your junk or spam folder too.

## Waiting for approval

If you see **You're registered and waiting for approval**, a coordinator still needs to approve your account. You get an email when this happens. If you have been waiting a while, press **Contact the community**.

## Identity check not finished

If you see that your identity verification is still in progress, press **Continue verification** to finish it.

## Two-step verification problems

Lost your phone? Press **Use backup code instead** and enter one of your backup codes. If you have none left, contact your coordinator.

## Adults only

If you see **This platform is for adults aged 18 and over**, the account belongs to someone under 18. If this is a mistake, [contact the community](/contact).

## Wrong community

If you belong to more than one community, check you chose the right **Community** on the sign-in page.

not_receiving_emails.title: I'm not receiving emails
not_receiving_emails.summary: Check your spam folder, the email address you used, and your notification settings.
not_receiving_emails.body:
If an email has not arrived, try these steps.

1. **Wait a few minutes.** Emails can take a little while to arrive.
2. **Look in your junk or spam folder.** If the email is there, mark it as not spam. This helps future emails reach your inbox.
3. **Check the email address.** Make sure you are using the address you signed up with.
4. **Ask for it again.** For a password reset, use [Forgot password?](/password/forgot). For email confirmation, try to sign in, then press **Resend verification email**.
5. **Check your notification settings.** If you are missing notification emails, open [Settings](/settings), choose the **Notifications** tab, and check the switches are on.

## Still nothing?

Some email services hold back messages from senders they do not know. Add your community's email address to your contacts or safe senders list.

If that does not help, [contact your community](/contact) and tell them which email you were expecting.

> Be careful with any email that asks for your password. Your community does not need your password to help you.

something_not_working.title: A page looks wrong or out of date
something_not_working.summary: Refresh the page, sign out and back in, or update your browser. Report the problem if it keeps happening.
something_not_working.body:
If a page looks out of date, shows an error, or a button does nothing, try these steps in order.

1. **Refresh the page.** Press your browser's reload button.
2. **Close and reopen.** If you saved the site to your home screen, or use the Android app, close it fully and open it again.
3. **Sign out and back in.** Open the menu under your name, press **Log Out**, then sign in again.
4. **Update your browser** to the latest version.
5. **Try another browser or device**, to see if the problem only happens in one place.

After the site is updated, you may see **This page was out of date and has been refreshed. Please sign in again.** This is normal. Sign in again and carry on.

## A page says Coming Soon

Some parts of the site are only switched on in some communities. If a page says **Coming Soon**, that part is not switched on in your community. Ask your community if you would like to use it.

If the problem keeps happening, please tell us. See **How do I report a problem?**

report_a_problem.title: How do I report a problem?
report_a_problem.summary: Use Report a problem to tell the support team about something that is broken. You get a reference number.
report_a_problem.body:
If something on the site is broken, or does not work as it should, you can send a report from the page where it happened.

1. Stay on the page with the problem.
2. Press **Report a problem**. On a computer, it is a button in the bottom right corner of the screen. On a phone, press **Menu** and find it near the bottom.
3. In **Short summary**, write a few words, for example "Save button does nothing".
4. In **What happened?**, describe what you did, what you expected, and what happened instead.
5. Under **Impact**, choose how much it affects you, from **I cannot continue** to **Visual or wording issue**.
6. Leave **Include technical diagnostics from this page** ticked. It helps the team find the fault.
7. Press **Send report**.

You then see **Report sent**, with a reference. Keep the reference, in case you want to ask about your report later.

You need to be signed in to send a report. If a page fails to load, the error screen may also show a **Report a problem** button.

> **Report a problem** is for technical faults. To report a member, a listing or a safety worry, see the **Privacy and safety** section.

contacting_your_community.title: How do I contact my community?
contacting_your_community.summary: Send a message to your community's team using the contact form.
contacting_your_community.body:
Your community has a team who can help with questions about your account, exchanges or anything else.

1. Open [Contact Us](/contact). You can also find **Contact Us** at the bottom of the page on a computer.
2. Enter your **Name** and **Email**.
3. Choose a **Subject**, such as **Account Help** or **Technical Issue**.
4. Write your **Message**.
5. Press **Send Message**.

Your message goes to your community's own contact address. They can reply to you by email.

## Other ways to get help

- For a technical fault, use **Report a problem**. See **How do I report a problem?**
- Read the [FAQ](/faq) and the rest of this [Help Centre](/help).
- If your community has the AI Assistant, it can answer general questions. See the **AI Assistant** section.

> If anyone is in immediate danger, contact your local emergency services first.

ai_assistant.title: AI Assistant
ai_assistant.summary: Ask questions about timebanking and your community, and get quick answers.

about_ai_assistant.title: What is the AI Assistant?
about_ai_assistant.summary: The AI Assistant answers questions about timebanking, your account and your community, in everyday language.
about_ai_assistant.body:
The **AI Assistant** is a chat tool. You type a question in everyday language, and it writes an answer. It is run by artificial intelligence (AI), not by a person.

## Where to find it

Open [AI Assistant](/chat). You can also find **AI Assistant** in the main menu. On a phone, press **Menu** and look under **Explore**.

## How to use it

1. Type your question in the box at the bottom of the page.
2. Press Enter, or press the send button. To start a new line without sending, hold Shift and press Enter.
3. Read the answer. Some answers include cards you can press, for example to open a listing or an event.

Not sure what to ask? Choose one of the examples under **Try asking...**.

Under each answer, press thumbs up or thumbs down to say whether it helped.

To clear the chat and start again, press the button to start a new conversation, at the top of the chat.

## Daily limit

You can ask a limited number of questions each day. The number you have left is shown at the top, for example **5 left today**.

ai_assistant_limits.title: What the AI Assistant can and can't do
ai_assistant_limits.summary: It can look things up for you, but it cannot take actions. It can make mistakes, so check anything important.
ai_assistant_limits.body:
## What it can do

The AI Assistant can look things up in your community and explain how things work. For example, it can:

- explain how timebanking works
- find listings, members and events that match what you ask
- find help articles, jobs or marketplace items, if your community uses them
- tell you your time credit balance

## What it cannot do

It can only look things up. It cannot act for you. It cannot:

- send or receive time credits
- send messages to other members
- create, change or delete listings
- change your settings or your account

To do these things, use the normal pages of the site.

## It can make mistakes

The AI Assistant can get things wrong, even when it sounds sure. Always check important details, such as dates, times and balances, on the page itself. For questions about your safety or your rights, ask a coordinator.

## Your privacy

Your questions are sent to an outside AI service so it can write an answer. Do not type passwords, bank details, health information or private details about other people. Your chat history is deleted if you delete your account.

listings.title: Offers and requests
listings.summary: Post what you can offer or what you need, and find listings from other members.

offers_and_requests.title: What are offers and requests?
offers_and_requests.summary: A listing tells the community what help you can give or what help you need.
offers_and_requests.body:
A listing is a short post that tells the community what you can do or what you need.

There are two kinds:

- An **Offer** is help you can give, such as gardening, a lift to the shops or help with a computer.
- A **Request** is help you would like to receive.

When someone helps you, you pay them in time credits. A time credit is one hour of someone's time. Every hour is worth the same, whatever the help is.

On the [Listings](/listings) page, each card shows whether it is **Offering** or **Requesting**, roughly how long it may take, and who posted it.

You can post both kinds. Many members offer one thing and ask for another.

A card may also show a **Mutual match** badge. This means that member wants something you offer and offers something you need.

> Your community can choose to accept only offers or only requests. If your listing is refused when you save it, ask your coordinator.

create_listing.title: How do I create a listing?
create_listing.summary: Post an offer or a request in a few steps from the Listings page.
create_listing.body:
You create a listing from the Listings page.

1. Open [Listings](/listings) and press **Create Listing**.
2. Under **Start with intent**, choose **Offer Help** or **Request Help**.
3. Type a **Title**. Be specific, for example "Weekly help with food shopping" rather than one word.
4. Write a **Description** of what you offer or need.
5. Choose a **Category**. Add **Skill Tags** if you like.
6. Under **Service delivery**, choose **In-person only**, **Remote only**, **Remote available** or **Depends on service**.
7. Enter the **Estimated Hours** one exchange may take.
8. Add a photo if you like.
9. Press **Create Listing**.

Your new listing then opens so you can check it.

If a field is missing or too short, a message appears under that field. Fix it and press **Create Listing** again.

The **Location** comes from your profile. To change it, update your location in your profile settings.

> If your community checks new listings first, your listing shows the status **Pending** until a coordinator approves it. Your community may also limit how many listings each member can have.

listing_ai_help.title: Using the AI writing help on a listing
listing_ai_help.summary: Get a draft description for your listing, then check it carefully before you save.
listing_ai_help.body:
If your community allows it, the listing form can write a draft description for you.

1. Type a **Title** first. The button stays greyed out until you do.
2. If you like, write a few notes in the **Description** box. The helper uses them.
3. Press **AI: Help me write this**.
4. Wait while the button shows **Generating...**.

The draft replaces whatever was in the **Description** box.

> Read the draft carefully before you save. It is written by a computer. It can make you sound more experienced, more available or more generous than you are, and it can add details you never gave. Change or delete anything that is not true.

A good description says what you will actually do, when you are usually free, and anything the other person should know.

If the helper is not available in your community, you will see a message saying the description could not be generated. You can write the description yourself.

listing_details.title: Categories, skill tags and optional details
listing_details.summary: Help the right members find your listing with a category, skill tags and extra details.
listing_details.body:
Categories and tags help members find your listing. Your community sets the list of categories.

- **Category**: choose the one that fits best. You can type to search the list. Your community may require a category.
- **Skill Tags**: type a skill and press Enter. You can add up to 10 tags.
- **Estimated Hours**: how long one exchange may take, between 0.5 and 100 hours.
- **Hours Available (optional)**: the total hours you are willing to give across all exchanges. Leave it blank for no limit. It cannot be less than the estimated hours.

## Optional service details

Open **Optional service details** to add:

- **Experience**, for example **Beginner-friendly** or **Professional / certified**.
- **Equipment**, for example **I'll provide everything needed** or **You'll need to provide your own**.
- **Accessibility Notes**, up to 200 characters, such as "step-free access".

When you save, these details are added to the end of your description, so everyone can read them.

listing_photo.title: Adding a photo to your listing
listing_photo.summary: Add one picture to make your listing easier to recognise.
listing_photo.body:
A photo can make your listing easier to recognise.

1. In the listing form, find **Add a photo**.
2. Press **Click to add a photo** and choose a picture from your device.
3. Check the preview. To remove it, press the cross in the corner of the preview.
4. Save the listing.

You can add one photo on this form. It must be a JPG, PNG or WebP file, and smaller than 8MB. If the file is too big, you will see **Image must be under 8MB**.

If the photo cannot be uploaded, your listing is still saved without it and a message tells you so. Edit the listing to try again.

To change the photo later, edit the listing, remove the old photo and add a new one.

Choose a picture you are happy for everyone in your community to see.

manage_listing.title: Editing, renewing or deleting your listing
manage_listing.summary: Change your listing, give it more time, see how it is doing, or remove it.
manage_listing.body:
Your own listings are on your profile, in the **Listings** tab. Open one to manage it.

When you view your own listing, these buttons appear near the title:

- **Edit** opens the form. Make your changes and press **Update Listing**.
- **Analytics** shows how many people viewed, contacted or saved the listing.
- **Renew Listing** appears when a listing has expired. **Extend** appears when a listing has an end date. Both give it more time.
- **Delete** removes the listing. Press **Delete listing** to confirm.

> Deleting a listing cannot be undone.

## Can I pause a listing?

There is no pause button. If you need a break, you can delete the listing and create it again later.

## Expiry

Your community may set listings to end after a while. The listing page shows the end date, for example "Expires" followed by the date. A listing can only be renewed a limited number of times. If renewing does not work, ask your coordinator.

browse_listings.title: Browsing and filtering listings
browse_listings.summary: Search listings and narrow them down by type, category, time and distance.
browse_listings.body:
Open [Listings](/listings) to see what members offer and need.

Type in the search box to look for words in the title, description, location or member's name, then press Enter.

Use the choices next to the search box:

- **Type**: **All Types**, **Offers** or **Requests**.
- **Category**: pick one, or keep **All Categories**.
- **Sort**: **Recommended** or **Newest first**.

Press **Filters** for more choices:

- **Duration**: **Quick (under 1h)**, **Short (1-3h)**, **Half day (3-6h)** or **Full day (6h+)**.
- **Service mode**: **Remote available** or **In-person only**.
- **Posted date**: **Today**, **This week** or **This month**.
- **Near me**: shows listings close to the location on your profile. Then choose a distance.

Press **Clear filters** to start again.

You can switch between grid and list layouts with the buttons at the top of the page.

> **Near me** uses the location on your profile. If you have not set one, you will see a message asking you to add it.

listing_map.title: Seeing listings on a map
listing_map.summary: If your community uses maps, view listings as pins on a map.
listing_map.body:
If your community uses maps, you can see listings as pins on a map.

1. Open [Listings](/listings).
2. Press the map button next to the grid and list buttons.
3. Press a pin to see the listing.
4. Press **View listing** to open it.

Only listings with a location appear on the map. If none have one, you will see **No listings with location data**.

A listing's location comes from the profile of the member who posted it. A listing page may also show a small map under **Service Location**.

Your listings use the location on your profile, so keep it up to date.

respond_to_listing.title: Responding to a listing
respond_to_listing.summary: Ask for help, send a message, save, share or comment on a listing.
respond_to_listing.body:
Open a listing to see the full details and who posted it. Under **Respond to this listing** you will find these buttons:

- **Request Exchange**: if your community uses exchange requests, this sends a request with the hours you propose. See the Exchanges section of this guide.
- **Send Message**: if your community does not use exchange requests, this opens a private conversation with the member instead.
- **Like** and **Comments**: show appreciation, or ask a question that everyone can see.
- **Save**: keeps the listing in your [Saved](/saved) items so you can find it again.
- **Share**: lets you share the listing or copy a link to it.
- **Report listing**: tells the community team about a problem.

If you already have an exchange for this listing, the first button shows **Exchange** and its current status instead.

Press the member's name to see their profile. It shows their reviews and other listings, under **More from** followed by their name.

report_listing.title: Reporting a listing
report_listing.summary: Tell your community team about a listing that looks unsafe, misleading or wrong.
report_listing.body:
Report a listing if it looks unsafe, misleading or does not belong in your community.

1. Open the listing.
2. Press **Report listing**.
3. Choose a reason: **Inappropriate content**, **Safety concern**, **Misleading description**, **Spam or scam**, **Not a timebank service** or **Other**.
4. Add **Additional details** if you can. This is optional, but it helps.
5. Press **Submit Report**.

You will see a thank-you message, and the button changes to **Reported**. You can report each listing only once.

Your community's moderators are told about the report and review it.

> If someone is in immediate danger, contact your local emergency services first.

finding_people.title: Finding people
finding_people.summary: Search the community, browse members, connect and see suggested matches.

member_directory.title: Browsing the member directory
member_directory.summary: Find members by name or area, and learn why some members are not listed.
member_directory.body:
The **Members** page lists people in your community.

1. Open [Members](/members).
2. Type a name in **Search members...** to find someone.
3. Choose **All Members**, **New Members** or **Most Active**, or pick an order under **Sort by**.
4. Press **Near me** to see members close to the location on your profile.
5. Press a member to open their profile.

## Why can't I see someone?

Not everyone is listed. The page may show a line such as "You are seeing 40 of the 55 people who have joined". Press **Why?** to see your community's rules.

A member may be missing because they chose not to be listed. Your community may also only list members who have finished their profile, added a photo or written an introduction. Everyone who is not shown is still a full member.

## Are you listed?

Press **Check whether you are listed**. It opens the **Privacy** tab of your settings. The **Search Engine Indexing** switch there also decides whether you appear in the member directory.

connections.title: Connecting with other members
connections.summary: Send, accept and manage connection requests with people you know.
connections.body:
A connection is a member you know and want to keep in touch with.

## Send a request

1. Open the member's profile.
2. Press **Connect**.

The button then shows **Cancel Request** until they answer.

## Answer a request

1. Open [Connections](/connections).
2. Choose the **Pending** tab.
3. Press **Accept** or **Decline**.

You can also press **Accept** on their profile.

## Manage your connections

- **My Connections** lists everyone you are connected to. Press **Message** to write to them, or **Disconnect** to remove them.
- **Sent** lists requests you have sent. Press **Cancel Request** to withdraw one.

On a connected member's profile, you can also open the **More options** menu (three dots) and choose **Remove Connection**.

search.title: Searching the community
search.summary: Find listings, members, events and groups in one search.
search.body:
Search looks for listings, members, events and groups in one place.

1. Open [Search](/search).
2. Type what you are looking for in **Search for anything...** and press **Search**.
3. Use the tabs to see all results, or only one kind. The tabs you see depend on what your community uses.

Press **Advanced Filters** to narrow the results by **Content Type**, **Category**, date, **Location** or **Skill Tags**, or to change **Sort By**.

## Saving a search

1. Press **Save this search**.
2. Type a name for it.
3. Press **Save**.

Your saved searches are listed under **Saved Searches**, so you can run them again.

If you find nothing, check your spelling, try broader words, or reset the filters.

explore_page.title: Using the Explore page
explore_page.summary: See popular listings, events, groups and new members in one place.
explore_page.body:
**Explore** is a starting point for finding out what is happening in your community. It opens a page called **Discover**.

Depending on what your community uses, you may see sections such as:

- **Popular Listings** and **Near You**
- **Upcoming Events** and **Active Groups**
- **Welcome Our Newest Members** and **People You May Know**, each with a **Connect** button
- **Trending Posts**, **Trending Hashtags** and **From the Blog**
- **Volunteer Opportunities** and **Organisations**

Press **See All** next to a section to open the full list.

The top of the page shows community figures, such as the number of members and the hours exchanged.

> If you cannot find **Explore** in the menu, your community is not using it.

matches.title: Your matches and suggestions
matches.summary: See listings, groups and volunteering that may suit you, based on your own listings.
matches.body:
The **Matches** page suggests listings, groups and volunteering opportunities that may suit you.

1. Open [Matches](/matches).
2. Use the tabs to show **All** matches or one kind.
3. Turn on **Mutual matches only** to see matches that work both ways: they want what you offer, and offer what you need.

Each card shows a match score and the main reasons. Some cards show **Why this score?** with more detail. Some include an explanation written by AI, which is labelled. Treat scores and explanations as a guide only.

On a card you can:

- press **Message** to write to the member;
- press **Save match** to keep it;
- press **Not interested** and choose a reason, so you see fewer matches like it;
- press **Join** on a group match.

## Getting better matches

Matches are based on your own listings. If you have none, the page asks you to **Create a listing**. Adding a location to your profile helps with distance.

match_preferences.title: Changing your match preferences
match_preferences.summary: Pause matching, set distance and quality, and choose how often you hear about matches.
match_preferences.body:
You can control how matching works for you.

1. Open [Matches](/matches) and press **Match preferences**.
2. Change the settings you want.
3. Press **Save preferences**.

The settings are:

- **Pause matching**: stops new suggestions and notifications until you turn it off again.
- **Maximum distance** and **Minimum match quality**, under **Distance & quality**.
- **Category interests**: tick the categories you want matches for. Leave them all unticked to match on every category.
- **Match digest frequency**: **Daily**, **Fortnightly**, **Monthly** or **Never**.
- **Hot match alerts**: be told straight away about very strong matches.
- **Mutual match alerts**: be told when a match works both ways.

Distance settings only work if your profile has a location.

skills_and_endorsements.title: Skills directory and endorsements
skills_and_endorsements.summary: Browse the skills members share, add your own, and endorse other members.
skills_and_endorsements.body:
The **Skills** page shows the skills members share, grouped by category.

1. Open [Skills](/skills).
2. Search for a skill, or open a category.
3. Choose a skill to see members who offer it (**Offers**) and members who want it (**Wants**).

## Adding your own skills

1. On the Skills page, press **Add your own skills**. This opens the **Skills** tab in your settings.
2. Press **Add Skill**.
3. Choose a skill and your level, such as **Beginner** or **Expert**.

## Endorsing someone

An endorsement is a quick way to say a member is good at a skill.

1. Open the member's profile.
2. Next to one of their skills, press the small endorse button. It says "Endorse" followed by the skill when you point at it.

Press it again to remove your endorsement. The number beside a skill shows how many members have endorsed it.

messages.title: Messages
messages.summary: Write privately to other members, send voice notes and understand safety notices.

start_conversation.title: Sending a private message
start_conversation.summary: Start a one-to-one conversation with another member.
start_conversation.body:
Messages are private conversations between you and one other member.

## Start a conversation

- From a profile: press **Send Message**.
- From the Messages page: open [Messages](/messages), press **New Message**, search for the member and choose them.
- From a listing: press **Send Message**, if your community shows it. The conversation then shows which offer or request it is about.

## Write and send

Type in **Type a message...** and press Enter, or press the send button. To start a new line, hold Shift and press Enter. A message can be up to 10,000 characters.

Your conversations are listed in the **Inbox** tab. Use **Search conversations...** to find one. Inside a conversation, the magnifier button searches its messages.

> If you see **Direct Messaging Disabled**, your community has turned off private messages. Use exchange requests instead. If you see **Messaging Restricted**, a community administrator has limited your messaging. Contact your coordinator if you think this is a mistake.

voice_and_attachments.title: Voice messages and attachments
voice_and_attachments.summary: Record a voice message or attach a picture or document.
voice_and_attachments.body:
You can send a recorded voice message or attach a file.

## Voice message

1. In a conversation, press the microphone button.
2. If your browser asks, allow it to use your microphone.
3. Speak. The screen shows **Recording...**.
4. Press **Stop** when you finish.
5. Listen back if you like. Press **Send**, or **Cancel** to throw it away.

If you see **Microphone Access Required**, allow the microphone in your browser settings and try again.

## Attachments

1. Press the paperclip button. On a phone, you may need to press the arrow first to show it.
2. Choose a file. You can attach pictures, PDF files, Word documents and text files.
3. Add a message if you like, then send.

To remove a file before you send it, press the cross next to it.

You can also react to a message with an emoji.

edit_delete_messages.title: Editing and deleting your messages
edit_delete_messages.summary: Change a message you sent, or remove it for you or for both of you.
edit_delete_messages.body:
You can change or remove messages you have sent.

## Edit a message

1. Point at your message, or press and hold it on a phone, and open the message options.
2. Choose **Edit**.
3. Change the text and press **Save**.

You can edit a message for up to 24 hours after you send it. An edited message shows **(edited)**. Voice messages cannot be edited.

## Delete a message

1. Open the message options and choose **Delete**.
2. Choose one of these:

- **Delete for everyone** removes the text for both of you. It is replaced by **[Message deleted]**.
- **Delete for me** hides it from your view only. The other member still sees it.

Press **Cancel** if you change your mind.

> Think before you send. The other person may read a message before you edit or delete it.

archive_delete_conversations.title: Removing or restoring a conversation
archive_delete_conversations.summary: Move a conversation out of your inbox, remove it for both of you, or bring it back.
archive_delete_conversations.body:
