1. Open [Achievements](/achievements).
2. Choose the **Challenges** tab.

Current challenges are listed under **Active Challenges**. Each one shows your progress and when it ends. You do not need to sign up. Your progress is counted as you take part.

When you finish a challenge, you are told. Press the **Claim** button, which shows the XP amount, to collect your reward. Some challenges also give a badge. Finished challenges move to **Completed**.

If you see **No active challenges**, there are none running right now.

## The XP Shop

The **XP Shop** tab lists rewards you can get with your XP. Your community's administrators decide what is on offer.

1. Check **Your balance**.
2. Press **Purchase** on an item.

Items you already have show **Owned**. If you need more XP, you are told how much.

If the shop is empty, your community has not added any rewards yet.

recognition_leaderboard.title: The leaderboard and community views
recognition_leaderboard.summary: See the most active members, your community's impact and your own journey.
recognition_leaderboard.body:
The [leaderboard](/leaderboard) page celebrates what your community does together. It has four tabs:

- **Most Active** ranks members
- **Community Impact** shows what the whole community has achieved
- **My Journey** shows your own progress over time
- **Spotlight** highlights members

## Using the rankings

On **Most Active**, choose what to rank by:

- **XP**
- **Volunteer Hours**
- **Credits Earned**
- **NexusScore**

Then choose a period: **All Time**, **This Season**, **This Month** or **This Week**.

Your own position is shown, for example **Your rank: #12 of 150 members**.

## Seasons

Some communities run seasons. A season is a set period of time with its own rewards. The season card shows how many days are left and your progress.

> There is currently no setting to remove yourself from the leaderboard.

recognition_nexus_score.title: What is my NexusScore?
recognition_nexus_score.summary: A score out of 1,000 that reflects how you take part in your community.
recognition_nexus_score.body:
Your NexusScore is a score out of 1,000. It sums up how you take part in your community. Open [NexusScore](/nexus-score) to see yours.

## What makes up the score

The score has six parts:

- **Community Engagement**, up to 250 points: giving and receiving time credits, your connections and how often you are active
- **Contribution Quality**, up to 200 points: your ratings and reviews
- **Volunteer Hours**, up to 200 points
- **Platform Activity**, up to 150 points: your listings, events, groups and how often you sign in
- **Badges & Achievements**, up to 100 points
- **Social Impact**, up to 100 points: your posts and the likes they receive

**Score Breakdown** shows how many points you have in each part. **How to improve** suggests what to do next.

## Tiers

As your score grows, you move through tiers, from **Novice** up to **Legendary**. The page shows your tier and how many points you need for the next one.

Press **Refresh** to update your score.

other_communities.title: Connecting with other communities
other_communities.summary: Meet members of partner communities, message them and exchange time credits.

federation_what_is_it.title: What does connecting with other communities mean?
federation_what_is_it.summary: Your community can partner with other communities, so members can meet and help each other.
federation_what_is_it.body:
Your community can form partnerships with other communities on the platform. This is called federation. When it is on, you can meet members of partner communities as well as your own.

Your community's administrators choose which communities to partner with. They also choose what each partnership allows. For example, one partner may allow messages, and another may also allow sending time credits.

## What you can do

Depending on the partnership, you can:

- see which communities your community is partnered with
- find members of those communities and view their profiles
- send them messages and connect with them
- browse their listings, events and groups
- send time credits to their members

## Taking part is your choice

You are not shown to other communities unless you choose to take part. You decide what they can see about you. See the article on joining in.

## If you see "Federation Not Available"

Your community has not switched this on. The page says **Contact your community admin to request federation access.** Ask your community's administrators if you would like it.

federation_join.title: How do I start connecting with other communities?
federation_join.summary: Choose to take part, and decide what partner communities can see about you.
federation_join.body:
You choose to take part from the [Federation](/federation) page.

## The guided set-up

The guided set-up lets you choose your privacy settings before anything is shared. It is the best way to start.

1. Open the [guided set-up](/federation/onboarding). You can also press **Set Up Federation** when you see it on a Federation page.
2. The set-up is called **Join the Federation**. It has four steps: **Welcome**, **Privacy**, **Communication** and **Confirm**.
3. On **Privacy**, choose what to share. For example, **Show my profile**, **Appear in search** and **Share my skills**.
4. On **Communication**, choose whether to allow messages and time credit transfers.
5. On **Confirm**, press **Enable Federation**.

If you are not ready, press **Do This Later**.

## The quick way

The [Federation](/federation) page also has an **Enable Federation** button. This turns everything on with standard settings: your profile is visible and searchable, and people can message you and send you time credits. Your location is not shared.

> If you use the quick button, check [Federation Settings](/federation/settings) straight afterwards and turn off anything you do not want.

federation_privacy.title: Choosing what other communities see, or stopping
federation_privacy.summary: Change your privacy settings for partner communities, or stop taking part.
federation_privacy.body:
You control what partner communities can see about you in [Federation Settings](/federation/settings).

## Profile Visibility

- **Show my profile** lets partner members see your profile.
- **Appear in search** lets them find you when they search.
- **Share my skills** shows your skills.
- **Share my location** shows your location. This is off unless you turn it on.
- **Show my reviews** shows reviews other members have left you.

## Communication

- **Allow messaging** lets partner members send you messages.
- **Allow transactions** lets partner members send you time credits.
- **Email notifications** sends you emails about activity from partner communities.

## Service Reach

Under **Service availability**, say whether you help **Local only**, are happy to help remotely (**Remote OK**), or **Will travel**. Set a **Travel radius** in kilometres.

Press **Save Settings** when you are done.

## Stopping

Press **Disable Federation**, either here or on the [Federation](/federation) page. On the Federation page you are asked to confirm: press **Yes, Disable**. You stop being visible to partner communities, and all your sharing settings are turned off.

You can start again later. If you do, check your settings again, because some may be switched back on.

federation_browse_message.title: Finding and messaging members of other communities
federation_browse_message.summary: Browse partner communities, their members and listings, and get in touch.
federation_browse_message.body:
Once you take part, the [Federation](/federation) page links to everything you can explore.

## Partner communities

Open [Partner Communities](/federation/partners) to see the communities your community is partnered with. Each one shows what the partnership allows, such as **Messaging** or **Transactions**. Press **Browse Members** or **Browse Listings** to see what they offer.

## Members

Open [Federation Members](/federation/members). Search by name or skill, or filter by community. Press **View Profile** to see a member, or **Send Message** to write to them.

On a member's profile you can also press **Connect** to ask to connect with them. Your connections with members of other communities are listed on [Federation Connections](/federation/connections), under **Connected**, **Received** and **Sent**. Press **Accept** to accept a request.

## Listings

[Federation Listings](/federation/listings) shows offers and requests from partner communities. Press **Contact** to message the person.

## Messages

Messages with partner members are kept on [Federation Messages](/federation/messages). Press **Compose Message** to write a new one.

## Events and groups

You can browse partner communities' events and groups. At the moment you cannot reply to their events or join their groups from here.

You can only message members who allow messages from other communities.

federation_send_credits.title: Sending time credits to someone in another community
federation_send_credits.summary: Pay a member of a partner community for help they gave you.
federation_send_credits.body:
You can send time credits to a member of a partner community, if both of you allow it.

1. Open the member's profile from [Federation Members](/federation/members).
2. Press **Send Credits**.
3. Enter the **Amount (hours)**. It must be a whole number from 1 to 100.
4. Add a **Description** saying what the credits are for. This is required.
5. Send the credits.

## When you cannot send credits

Sending only works when all of these are true:

- you have switched on **Allow transactions** in [Federation Settings](/federation/settings)
- the other member has switched it on too
- the partnership between your communities allows transactions

If the member does not accept transfers, you see **This member does not accept federated credit transfers.**

> Only send credits for help you have agreed with the member. Check the name and amount before you send.

volunteering.title: Volunteering
volunteering.summary: Find volunteering opportunities, apply, log your hours and earn time credits.

how_volunteering_works.title: How does volunteering work?
how_volunteering_works.summary: Apply to an opportunity, log the hours you give, and get time credits once they are approved.
how_volunteering_works.body:
Volunteering lets you give your time to local organisations and earn time credits for it. A time credit is one hour of time, the same currency you use in your wallet.

It works in four steps:

1. Find an opportunity and apply.
2. The organisation approves your application.
3. You log the hours you give.
4. The organisation approves your hours, and time credits are added to your wallet.

## Finding the volunteering page

Open the **Community** menu and choose **Volunteering**, or go to [Volunteering](/volunteering).

The page has tabs:

- **Opportunities** lists everything you can apply for.
- **My Applications** shows the applications you have sent.
- **My Hours** shows the hours you have logged.
- **Certificates** lets you create a record of your approved hours.

Your community may have extra sections too, such as **Wellbeing**, **Projects** or **Donations**. Press **More** to see them, and **Show fewer** to hide them again. On a phone, the sections appear in a drop-down list instead of tabs.

> Your community chooses which sections to show. If you cannot see one described in this guide, your community has not switched it on.

finding_volunteer_opportunities.title: How do I find a volunteering opportunity?
finding_volunteer_opportunities.summary: Search and filter the opportunities posted by local organisations.
finding_volunteer_opportunities.body:
You find opportunities on the **Opportunities** tab of the [Volunteering](/volunteering) page.

1. Open [Volunteering](/volunteering).
2. Type in the **Search opportunities...** box. It looks at titles, descriptions, places, skills and organisation names.
3. Use the filters to look for opportunities near you or ones you can do **Remote**, which means online or by phone.
4. Press **Load more** to see more results.

Each card shows the organisation, the title, where it takes place, the dates and the skills needed.

## Looking at an opportunity

Press **View Details** to open the full opportunity. It shows the description, the organisation, the dates and the skills needed.

If you see **No opportunities found**, try a different search word or check back later.

> The organisation name on a card may link to the organisation's own page. There you can see its other opportunities and read reviews.

applying_to_volunteer.title: How do I apply to volunteer?
applying_to_volunteer.summary: Send an application, follow its progress and withdraw it if your plans change.
applying_to_volunteer.body:
You apply with the **Apply** button on an opportunity card, or **Apply Now** on the opportunity's own page.

1. Press **Apply** or **Apply Now**.
2. Add a short message if you like. Tell the organisation why you would like to help.
3. Press **Submit Application**.

The card then shows **Applied**. The organisation is told about your application.

## Following your application

Open the **My Applications** tab on the [Volunteering](/volunteering) page. Each application shows one of these:

- **Pending**: the organisation has not decided yet.
- **Approved**: you have been accepted. You can now log hours for this organisation.
- **Declined**: the organisation did not accept this application.

The organisation may add a note. It appears as **Organiser's note:**. You get a notification when they decide.

## Withdrawing an application

You can withdraw an application while it is **Pending**. Press **Withdraw** on the application. There is no second question, so check first. You cannot withdraw an application once it is approved. Contact the organisation instead.

If your application was declined or withdrawn, you can apply again later.

> Some communities have safeguarding rules about who can contact whom. If one of these applies, you see a message when you try to apply.

logging_volunteer_hours.title: How do I log my volunteering hours?
logging_volunteer_hours.summary: Record the time you gave so the organisation can approve it and pay you time credits.
logging_volunteer_hours.body:
You log hours on the **My Hours** tab of the [Volunteering](/volunteering) page.

1. Open [Volunteering](/volunteering) and choose the **My Hours** tab.
2. Press **Log Hours**.
3. Choose the **Organisation** you volunteered for.
4. Enter the **Date**.
5. Enter the **Hours**, for example 3.5.
6. Add a note about what you did, if you like.
7. Press **Log Hours**.

You see **Hours logged successfully!**

## Rules for logging hours

- Each entry must be between a quarter of an hour and 24 hours.
- You cannot log a date in the future, or more than 90 days ago.
- You can make one entry per organisation per day.
- You can only choose organisations that have approved your application, or that you belong to.

## Getting your time credits

New hours show as **Awaiting approval**. The organisation then approves or declines them. In some communities, hours are approved straight away.

When hours are approved, time credits go into your wallet automatically. You get a notification.

> Credits are paid for whole hours only. For example, 3.5 approved hours gives you 3 time credits. An entry of less than one hour gives no credits. If you can, log a longer session as one entry.

If hours are declined, you get a notification. Talk to the organisation if you think there is a mistake.

volunteer_hours_and_certificates.title: Seeing your hours and getting a certificate
volunteer_hours_and_certificates.summary: Check your approved hours and create a certificate that lists them.
volunteer_hours_and_certificates.body:
Your **My Hours** tab shows a summary of the time you have given.

- **Approved & credited**: hours the organisation has approved.
- **Awaiting approval**: hours still waiting for a decision.
- **Total Hours**: both added together.

Below the figures you can see **Hours by Organisation** and **Hours by Month**. These count approved hours only.

## Creating a certificate

A certificate is a record of all your approved volunteering hours, across every organisation. You might use it for a job application or a course.

1. Open [Volunteering](/volunteering).
2. Choose the **Certificates** tab.
3. Press **Generate Certificate**.
4. You see **Certificate generated!**

Each certificate shows your verified hours, the dates they cover and the hours for each organisation.

> Only approved hours count. If none of your hours are approved yet, you see a message saying so. Ask the organisation to review your hours first.

A new certificate includes any hours approved since your last one, so you can create a fresh one whenever you need it.

volunteer_wellbeing.title: Checking in on your wellbeing
volunteer_wellbeing.summary: Record how you feel and get suggestions about when to take a break.
volunteer_wellbeing.body:
If your community uses it, the **Wellbeing** section helps you notice when you might be doing too much.

1. Open [Volunteering](/volunteering).
2. Press **More**, then choose **Wellbeing**.
3. Press **Log How I'm Feeling**.
4. Choose a mood: **Struggling**, **Low**, **Okay**, **Good** or **Great**.
5. Add a note if you like.
6. Press **Submit Check-in**.

You see **Mood check-in recorded.**

## What the page shows you

- A **Wellbeing Score** out of 100.
- How much you have volunteered this week and this month.
- Your recent check-ins.
- Suggested rest days, and self-care tips.

If the page shows a burnout warning, please take it seriously. Rest is part of volunteering well.

> Community administrators can see when the system thinks a volunteer may be at risk of burnout. This is so they can offer support. If you are struggling, you can also talk to the organisation or your community coordinator directly.

volunteer_training_and_incidents.title: Recording training and reporting an incident
volunteer_training_and_incidents.summary: Add your safeguarding training and report a safeguarding incident while volunteering.
volunteer_training_and_incidents.body:
If your community uses it, the **Safeguarding** section lets you keep a record of your training. You can also report an incident that happened while you were volunteering.

Open [Volunteering](/volunteering), press **More**, then choose **Safeguarding**.

## Adding a training record

1. Choose **Training Records** and press **Add Training**.
2. Choose the **Training Type**.
3. Fill in the **Training Name** and the **Provider**.
4. Enter the **Date Completed** and any **Expiry Date**.
5. Press **Save Record**.

The record starts as **Pending**. A community administrator checks it and marks it **Verified** or **Rejected**.

## Reporting an incident

1. Choose **Incident Reports** and press **Report Incident**.
2. Give it a **Title**.
3. Describe what happened in **Description**. Use at least 20 characters.
4. Choose the **Severity** and a **Category**.
5. Press **Report Incident**.

You see **Incident reported.** Community administrators handle incident reports. The status changes as they work on it, for example **Investigating** or **Resolved**.

> If someone is in immediate danger, contact your local emergency services first. Do not wait for a reply here.

community_projects.title: Proposing or supporting a community project
community_projects.summary: Suggest a volunteer project for your community, or show support for one.
community_projects.body:
If your community uses it, the **Projects** section lets members suggest volunteer projects.

Open [Volunteering](/volunteering), press **More**, then choose **Projects**.

## Proposing a project

1. Press **Propose a Project**.
2. Fill in the **Title** and **Description**.
3. Add a **Category**, a **Location**, the **Target Volunteers** and a **Proposed Date** if you know them.
4. Press **Propose**.

You see **Project proposed successfully!** Community administrators review each proposal. Its status then changes, for example to **Under Review**, **Approved** or **Rejected**.

## Supporting a project

Each project card has a support button and shows how many supporters it has. Press it to add your support. Press it again to remove your support.

Each card also shows how many volunteers the project still needs.

volunteering_donations.title: Donating money to your community
volunteering_donations.summary: Give money by card or record a pledge. This is separate from time credits.
volunteering_donations.body:
If your community uses it, the **Donations** section lets you give money to support the community. Money donations are not the same as time credits. You earn time credits by giving time.

Open [Volunteering](/volunteering), press **More**, then choose **Donations**.

## Donating by card

1. Press **Donate by card**.
2. Enter the **Amount** and choose the **Currency**.
3. Choose a **Fund** if you want your money used for something in particular.
4. Add a message, or choose **Donate anonymously**, if you like.
5. Press **Continue to Payment**.
6. Enter your card details and pay.

When the payment works, you see **Thank You!** Press **View Receipt** to see your receipt.

## Recording a pledge

If you plan to pay another way, such as by bank transfer:

1. Press **Pledge by bank transfer**.
2. Enter the **Amount** and **Payment method**.
3. Press **Record Pledge**.

Your pledge shows as **Pending** until a community administrator confirms the money has arrived.

## Giving days and your history

**Active Giving Days** shows any fundraising campaigns running now. **My Donations** lists what you have given.

organisations.title: Organisations
organisations.summary: Find local organisations, volunteer with them, or register and run your own.

browsing_organisations.title: How do I find an organisation?
browsing_organisations.summary: Browse the charities, groups and partners that offer volunteering in your community.
browsing_organisations.body:
You find organisations on the **Organisations** page. Open the **Community** menu and choose **Organisations**, or go to [Organisations](/organisations).

1. Browse the list, or type in **Search organisations...**.
2. Press an organisation to open its page.

Only organisations your community has approved appear here.

## On an organisation's page

- A description of the organisation.
- How many **Opportunities**, **Volunteers** and **Hours Logged** it has.
- Its star rating and **Reviews**, if your community uses reviews.
- **Active Opportunities**, the volunteering you can apply for now.

Press **Website** to visit the organisation's website. Press **Contact** to send it an email from your own email program.

## Volunteering with an organisation

There is no button to join an organisation directly. You volunteer by applying to one of its opportunities.

1. Find the opportunity under **Active Opportunities**.
2. Press **Apply**.
3. Add a message if you like, and press **Submit Application**.

Follow your application on the **My Applications** tab of the [Volunteering](/volunteering) page.

reviewing_an_organisation.title: How do I review an organisation?
reviewing_an_organisation.summary: Share your experience of volunteering with an organisation.
reviewing_an_organisation.body:
If your community uses reviews, you can review an organisation you have volunteered with.

1. Open the organisation's page from [Organisations](/organisations).
2. Go to **Reviews** and press **Write review**.
3. Choose a **Rating** from 1 to 5 stars.
4. Write a **Comment**. Say what worked well or what others should know.
5. Press **Submit review**.

You see **Review submitted.**

## Who can leave a review

The **Write review** button is shown to everyone. But you can only send a review if you have really volunteered with that organisation. This means it approved your application, or approved hours you logged. If not, you see a message and the review is not saved.

You can leave one review for each organisation.

> Please keep reviews fair and about your own experience. Your community's guidelines apply to reviews too.

registering_an_organisation.title: How do I register my organisation?
registering_an_organisation.summary: Add your charity, group or business so you can post volunteering opportunities.
registering_an_organisation.body:
Any member can ask to register an organisation. A community administrator then approves it.

1. Go to [Register Organisation](/organisations/register), or press **Register Organisation** on the Organisations page.
2. Enter the **Organisation Name**. It must be at least 3 characters.
3. Write a **Description** of at least 20 characters. Say what the organisation does and what volunteers would help with.
4. Enter a **Contact Email**.
5. Add a website under **Website (optional)** if you have one. It must start with http:// or https://.
6. Read the **Organisation Registration Terms**.
7. Tick **I have read and agree to the organisation registration terms above.**
8. Press **Register Organisation**.

You see **Organisation Registered!** You are taken to [My Organisations](/volunteering/my-organisations).

## What happens next

Your organisation shows under **Pending Approval** until an administrator reviews it. The administrators are told about your request.

- If it is approved, it appears on the Organisations page. You can then post opportunities and approve volunteers.
- If it is not approved, it shows under **Declined**. Contact your community administrator to find out why.

> If you see **Failed to register organisation. Please try again.**, the name may already be in use. Try a slightly different name, or ask your community administrator.

managing_your_organisation.title: Managing your organisation's dashboard
managing_your_organisation.summary: Where organisation owners review applications, approve hours and see their volunteers.
managing_your_organisation.body:
If you run an approved organisation, you manage it from its dashboard.

1. Open [My Organisations](/volunteering/my-organisations).
2. Press **Manage** on your organisation.

You can also press **Manage this organisation** on the organisation's own page.

## The dashboard tabs

- **Overview** shows your figures, such as **Pending Applications** and **Hours Pending Review**. It also has quick buttons for the most common tasks.
- **Applications** lists people who want to volunteer. Approve or decline them here.
- **Hours Review** lists hours your volunteers have logged. Approve or decline them here.
- **Volunteers** shows your **Volunteer Roster** and the hours each person has given.
- **Wallet** shows your organisation's time-credit record.
- **Settings** lets you change the name, description, contact email and website. Press **Save Changes** when you are done.

> Only the owner and administrators of an organisation can use its dashboard. If you see **Access Denied**, you do not manage this organisation.

posting_a_volunteer_opportunity.title: How do I post a volunteering opportunity?
posting_a_volunteer_opportunity.summary: Ask for volunteers by posting an opportunity for your organisation.
posting_a_volunteer_opportunity.body:
You need an approved organisation to post an opportunity. If you do not have one yet, [register your organisation](/organisations/register) first.

1. Go to [Post Opportunity](/volunteering/create). You can also press **Post Opportunity** on your dashboard.
2. Choose your **Organisation**.
3. Enter an **Opportunity Title** of at least 5 characters.
4. Write a **Description** of at least 20 characters. Say what volunteers will do and anything they need.
5. Enter the **Location**, or tick **Remote opportunity** if people can help online or by phone.
6. List the **Skills Needed**, if any.
7. Choose a **Start Date** and **End Date** if the opportunity has them.
8. Press **Post Opportunity**.

You see **Opportunity posted successfully!** Your opportunity goes live straight away. Members can find it on the [Volunteering](/volunteering) page.

## When people apply

You get a notification and an email each time someone applies. Review applications on the **Applications** tab of your dashboard.

> If you see **No Approved Organisation**, your organisation is still waiting for approval, or you do not manage one.

approving_volunteers_and_hours.title: Approving volunteers and their hours
approving_volunteers_and_hours.summary: Accept applications and approve logged hours so volunteers receive time credits.
approving_volunteers_and_hours.body:
As an organisation owner, you approve people who apply, and the hours they log.

## Approving applications

1. Open your dashboard from [My Organisations](/volunteering/my-organisations).
2. Choose the **Applications** tab.
3. Press **Approve** or **Decline** on each application. You can also use **Approve All** or **Decline All**.
4. When you decline, you can add a **Decision note** to explain why.

The volunteer is told your decision.

## Approving hours

1. Choose the **Hours Review** tab.
2. Check each entry: who, when and how many hours.
3. Press **Approve** or **Decline**.

When you approve hours, the volunteer receives time credits in their wallet straight away. You do not need to pay them separately.

> Credits are paid for whole hours only. For example, 2.5 approved hours pays 2 time credits. An entry under one hour pays nothing.

You cannot approve hours you logged yourself. Please review hours promptly. Volunteers see them as **Awaiting approval** until you decide.

organisation_wallet.title: How does an organisation's wallet work?
organisation_wallet.summary: See the time credits your organisation has given out, and add credits if you choose.
organisation_wallet.body:
Each organisation has a **Wallet** that records the time credits it has given to volunteers.

Open your dashboard from [My Organisations](/volunteering/my-organisations) and choose the **Wallet** tab.

## Paying volunteers

You pay volunteers by approving their hours. The credits are added to their wallet automatically. There is no separate payment button.

You do not need credits in the organisation's wallet first. The balance can go below zero. A negative balance shows how many credits your organisation has given out.

## Adding credits

You can move credits from your own wallet into the organisation's wallet.

1. Press **Deposit Credits**.
2. Enter the **Amount (hours)**. Use whole numbers only, up to 1,000.
3. Add a note if you like.
4. Press **Deposit**.

The credits leave your personal wallet. If you do not have enough, the deposit fails.

## Transaction History

**Transaction History** lists every deposit, volunteer payment and adjustment.

> Members cannot see your organisation's wallet balance. Only the people who manage the organisation can.

jobs.title: Jobs
jobs.summary: Find paid, volunteer and time-credit roles, apply, and post your own vacancies.

finding_jobs.title: How do I find a job vacancy?
finding_jobs.summary: Search and filter the paid, volunteer and time-credit roles in your community.
finding_jobs.body:
You find vacancies on the **Job Vacancies** page. Open the **Community** menu and choose **Jobs**, or go to [Jobs](/jobs).

1. Type in **Search vacancies...** to look for a word in the title, description or skills.
2. Use the filters to narrow the list.
3. Press **Load More** at the bottom to see more.

## Filters

- **Sort by**: **Newest**, **Closing Soon** or **Highest Salary**.
- **Remote Only**: show roles you can do from home.
- Job type: **Paid**, **Volunteer** or **Timebank**. A timebank role pays in time credits rather than money.
- Commitment: **Full Time**, **Part Time**, **Flexible** or **One-off**.

## Reading a job card

Each card shows the title, who posted it, the location and the pay if there is any. **Featured** jobs are shown first. A card may say **Closes in** a number of days when the deadline is near.

If you have already applied, the card shows **Applied**.

> Only open jobs with a deadline in the future appear in the list.

job_details_and_saving.title: Looking at a job and saving it for later
job_details_and_saving.summary: Read the full details, check how well your skills match, and save or share a job.
job_details_and_saving.body:
Press a job to open its page. It shows everything you need to decide whether to apply.

- **About this role**: the full description.
- **Skills Required**: the skills the poster wants.
- **Application Deadline**: the last day to apply.
- The pay, **Hours per Week** and any **Time Credits**.
- **Contact Information**, if the poster added it.

## Checking your skills

If the job lists skills, you may see a skills match. This compares the job with the skills on your profile. Press **Am I Qualified?** to see which skills you have and which ones you could develop.

Keep your profile skills up to date to get a more useful match.

## Saving a job

Press the bookmark button at the top of the job page. You see **Job saved**. Find your saved jobs on the **Saved Jobs** tab of the [Jobs](/jobs) page. Press the button again to remove it.

## Sharing a job

Press **Share** and choose **Copy Link** or **Share via Email**. On some phones you also see **Share...**, which opens your phone's sharing options.

Press **Back to Jobs** to return to the list.

applying_for_a_job.title: How do I apply for a job?
applying_for_a_job.summary: Send a message and your CV to the person who posted the vacancy.
applying_for_a_job.body:
You apply from the job's own page.

1. Open the job from [Jobs](/jobs).
2. Press **Apply Now**.
3. Write a message under **Your message (optional)**. Say why you are a good fit.
4. Add your CV if you like. It can be a PDF, DOC or DOCX file, up to 5MB.
5. Press **Submit Application**.

You see **Application submitted successfully!** The person who posted the job is told straight away. You get a confirmation email.

> Some communities ask for a message with every application, or do not accept CVs. If so, the form tells you.

## Applying again quickly

After your first application, your message is remembered. Next time you may see **Quick Apply with Saved Profile**, which sends it again in one step. You can also start a fresh message.

## When you cannot apply

- **You've already applied** means you have sent an application already. You can apply only once to each job.
- **No longer accepting applications** means the job has closed or the deadline has passed.
- **This is your vacancy** means you posted it yourself.

After applying, press **Message Employer** on the job page to send the poster a message.

tracking_job_applications.title: Tracking and withdrawing your applications
tracking_job_applications.summary: See where each application has got to, and withdraw one if you change your mind.
tracking_job_applications.body:
You follow your applications on the **My Applications** page. Press **My Applications** at the top of the [Jobs](/jobs) page, or go to [My Applications](/jobs/my-applications).

Each application shows its status. For example:

- **Pending**: the poster has not looked at it yet.
- **Screening**: the poster is reviewing it.
- **Interview**: you have been asked to an interview.
- **Offer**: you have been offered the role.
- **Accepted** or **Rejected**: a decision has been made.

Press **Status History** to see each change and when it happened. You get a notification when your status changes.

## Withdrawing an application

1. Find the application.
2. Press **Withdraw**.
3. Check the message and confirm.

You see **Application withdrawn**.

> Withdrawing cannot be undone. You cannot apply to the same job again afterwards. Any interview is cancelled, and any offer is withdrawn.

## Your job data

Press **Download my data** to save a copy of your job applications and related information as a file.

job_interviews_and_offers.title: Responding to an interview or a job offer
job_interviews_and_offers.summary: Accept or decline interview invitations and job offers.
job_interviews_and_offers.body:
When a poster invites you to an interview or makes you an offer, you are told by notification. You respond on the [My Applications](/jobs/my-applications) page.

## Interviews

The application shows the interview date, time, type and length. The status says **Interview Requested**.

- Press **Accept** to confirm. The status changes to **Interview Confirmed**.
- Press **Decline** if you cannot attend.
- Press **Add to Calendar** to save the date to your calendar.
- For video interviews, use the join button at the time of the interview.

You also get reminders before the interview.

## Offers

The application shows **You received an offer!** with the details, such as the salary and start date.

- Press **Accept Offer** to accept.
- Press **Decline** to turn it down.

> For **Timebank** roles, accepting an offer moves the job's time credits from the poster's wallet to yours straight away. If the poster does not have enough credits, accepting will not work. Talk to the poster if this happens.

Accepting an offer marks the role as filled.

job_alerts.title: How do I get alerts about new jobs?
job_alerts.summary: Set up a job alert and hear about new vacancies that match what you want.
job_alerts.body:
A job alert tells you when a new vacancy matching your choices is posted.

1. Go to [Job Alerts](/jobs/alerts), or press **Job Alerts** on the Jobs page.
2. Press **Create Alert**.
3. Enter **Keywords**, separated by commas. For example, gardening, teaching.
4. Add **Categories** if you like.
5. Choose a **Job Type** and **Commitment Level**, or leave them as **Any**.
6. Add a **Location**, or tick **Remote positions only**.
7. Press **Create Alert**.

When a matching vacancy is posted, you get a notification and an email.

## Managing your alerts

Each alert shows when it was created and when it last found a job.

- Press the pause button to stop an alert for a while. It shows **Paused**. Press it again to restart it.
- Press the delete button to remove an alert. You are asked to confirm.

> An alert matches when at least one keyword appears in the job title or description. Use a few simple words to get better results.

posting_a_job_vacancy.title: How do I post a job vacancy?
posting_a_job_vacancy.summary: Advertise a paid, volunteer or time-credit role to your community.
posting_a_job_vacancy.body:
Any member can post a vacancy.

1. Press **Post Vacancy** on the [Jobs](/jobs) page, or go to [Post a Job Vacancy](/jobs/create).
2. Enter a **Job Title** and **Description**.
3. Choose the **Job Type**: **Paid**, **Volunteer** or **Timebank**.
4. Choose the **Commitment**, and add a **Category** and **Location**.
5. List the **Skills Required**, separated by commas.
6. Add the **Hours per Week**.
7. For a timebank role, enter the **Time Credits Offered**.
8. For a paid role, fill in the **Compensation** section, or tick **Salary is negotiable**.
9. Choose an **Application Deadline**. If you leave it empty, a deadline is set for you.
10. Press **Post Vacancy**.

Press **Preview** first to see how it will look. Press **Save as Draft** to finish it later.

> The **Contact Email** and **Contact Phone** you enter are shown to everyone who can see the job. Only add details you are happy to share.

## Checks before a job goes live

In some communities an administrator checks new vacancies first. Your job then stays as **Draft** until it is approved. You get a notification when it is approved or rejected.

First time posting? Press **Start Wizard** on the Jobs page for a step-by-step guide.

managing_your_vacancy.title: Managing a vacancy you posted
managing_your_vacancy.summary: Edit, close, reopen, renew or delete your vacancy, and see how it is doing.
managing_your_vacancy.body:
Your vacancies are on the **My Postings** tab of the [Jobs](/jobs) page. Each one shows its status: **Open**, **Closed**, **Filled** or **Draft**.

Open one of your jobs to manage it. The page shows **You posted this vacancy** and your options.

- **Edit**: change the details. Press **Save Changes** when done.
- **Close Vacancy**: stop new applications. You can reopen it later.
- **Reopen**: make a closed vacancy visible again.
- **Renew**: extend the deadline by 7, 14, 30 or 60 days. This appears when the deadline has passed or the job is closed.
- **Analytics**: see views, applications and other figures.
- **Delete**: remove the vacancy.

> Deleting is permanent. It also deletes every application, interview and offer for that job. If you only want to stop applications, use **Close Vacancy** instead.

## Reminders

You get a reminder 7 days before your deadline. Open vacancies that have not been changed for a long time may be closed automatically.

reviewing_job_applicants.title: Reviewing applicants for your vacancy
reviewing_job_applicants.summary: Move applicants through the stages, invite them to interview and make an offer.
reviewing_job_applicants.body:
You get a notification and an email each time someone applies. Their applications are listed on your job's page, under **Applications**.

## Moving applicants through the stages

Each application has buttons for the next step, such as **Screening**, **Interview**, **Accepted** or **Rejected**. The applicant is told when their status changes. Press **Message** to send an applicant a message.

## Using the Kanban Board

Press **Kanban Board** on your job page. It shows your applicants in columns, one for each stage. Drag a card to move it to another stage.

On each card you can:

- Press **Download CV** to see the applicant's CV.
- Press **Schedule Interview**. Choose the type, date, time and place or meeting link, then press **Send Interview Request**.
- Press **Send Offer**. Enter the salary, start date and a message, then send it.

The applicant can accept or decline your interview request or offer. You are told when they do.

> For **Timebank** roles, the time credits move from your wallet to the applicant when they accept your offer. Make sure you have enough credits before you send it.

You can send one offer to each applicant.

marketplace.title: Marketplace
marketplace.summary: Buy, sell and give away items with other members of your community.

browsing_the_marketplace.title: How do I find things in the marketplace?
browsing_the_marketplace.summary: Browse, search and filter the items other members are selling or giving away.
browsing_the_marketplace.body:
The marketplace is where members buy, sell and give away items. It is separate from timebanking, where you swap time.

Open the **Community** menu and choose **Marketplace**, or go to [Marketplace](/marketplace).

## Searching

1. Type in **Search marketplace...**.
2. Press a category to see only that kind of item. Press **All** to see everything again.
3. Press **Load More** to see more listings.

**Featured Listings** appear at the top.

## Advanced search

Under **Quick Links**, press **Advanced Search**, or go to [Advanced Search](/marketplace/search). Here you can filter by:

- **Category**
- **Price Range**
- **Condition**, such as **New** or **Good**
- How you get the item, such as **Pickup Only**
- How recently it was posted

Press **Reset Filters** to clear your choices.

## Free items

To see only items members are giving away, go to [Free Items](/marketplace/free).

If you see **No Listings Found**, nobody has listed anything that matches yet.

looking_at_a_listing.title: Looking at an item and contacting the seller
looking_at_a_listing.summary: Read the details of an item, see who is selling it and send them a message.
looking_at_a_listing.body:
Press an item to open its page. It shows the photos, price, condition, location and description. It also shows how you get the item, such as **Pickup Only**.

A listing may show extra labels:

- **Negotiable**: the seller is open to offers.
- **Free**: the item is being given away.

## The seller

The seller's card shows their name and when they joined. Press **View Profile** to see their other listings.

## Asking the seller a question

1. Press **Message Seller**.
2. Your messages open with a note ready to send, saying you are interested in this item.
3. Add your question and send it.

It is a good idea to agree how and where to collect the item before you buy.

## Your next step

- To pay the asking price, press **Buy Now**.
- To suggest a different price, press **Make Offer**.

Items marked **Negotiable** have no **Buy Now** button. You make an offer instead.

> Meet in a public place when you collect an item, or bring someone with you. Never share your bank or card details in a message.

selling_an_item.title: How do I sell or give away an item?
selling_an_item.summary: Create a listing with photos, a price and how the buyer gets the item.
selling_an_item.body:
You list an item from the **Sell Something** page.

1. Press **Sell Something** on the [Marketplace](/marketplace), or go to [Sell Something](/marketplace/sell).
2. Add **Photos**. You can drag them in or press to choose them. The first photo is the cover.
3. Under **Details**, enter a **Title** and **Description**.
4. Choose a **Category** and the **Condition**.
5. Under **Pricing**, choose the **Price Type**: **Fixed Price**, **Negotiable** or **Free**.
6. Enter the **Price** and **Currency**, unless the item is free.
7. Under **Location & Delivery**, enter the **Location**.
8. Choose the **Delivery Method**.
9. Press **Publish Listing**.

You see **Listing created successfully!**

## Choosing a delivery method

Choose **Pickup Only** if the buyer will collect the item. Many communities do not allow items to be posted. If yours does not, choosing a posting option stops the listing being published. You see a message explaining this.

## Before your listing appears

In many communities, an administrator checks new listings first. Your listing will not appear to others until it is approved. If it is not approved, you get a notification with the reason.

> Only list items you own and are allowed to sell. Describe the condition honestly, and include any faults in the photos.

managing_your_listings.title: Managing your listings
managing_your_listings.summary: Edit, renew or remove the items you have listed.
managing_your_listings.body:
Your listings are on the **My Listings** page. Under **Quick Links** on the marketplace, press **My Listings**, or go to [My Listings](/marketplace/my-listings).

The tabs show your **Active**, **Sold** and **Expired** listings.

## Editing a listing

1. Press **Edit** on the listing.
2. Make your changes.
3. Press **Save Changes**.

In communities that check listings, changing the details or photos sends the listing back to be checked again.

## Renewing a listing

Listings expire after a set time. Expired listings move to the **Expired** tab. Press **Renew** to list the item again.

## Removing a listing

1. Press **Remove** on the listing.
2. Confirm that you want to remove it.

This cannot be undone.

> When you have sold or given away an item, remove its listing. Otherwise other members may still try to buy it.

making_an_offer.title: Making and answering offers
making_an_offer.summary: Suggest a price to a seller, or accept, decline or counter an offer you receive.
making_an_offer.body:
An offer lets a buyer suggest a different price.

## Making an offer

1. Open the item and press **Make Offer**.
2. Enter **Your Offer**. The **Asking price:** is shown for comparison.
3. Add a message if you like.
4. Press **Send Offer**.

You see **Offer sent successfully!** The seller is told. An offer expires after 2 days if the seller does not answer. You can make one offer at a time on each item.

## Following your offers

Go to [My Offers](/marketplace/my-offers). The **Sent** tab shows offers you made. The **Received** tab shows offers on your items.

Each offer shows its status: **Pending**, **Accepted**, **Declined**, **Countered**, **Withdrawn** or **Expired**. While an offer is **Pending**, you can press **Withdraw** to cancel it.

## Answering an offer on your item

- Press **Accept** to agree the price.
- Press **Decline** to turn it down.
- Press **Counter** to suggest another price. Enter the **Counter Amount** and press **Send Counter**.

If a seller counters your offer, press **Accept Counter** to agree.

## After an offer is accepted

The item is held for the buyer for 2 days. The buyer pays with **Pay accepted offer** on the offer. If they do not pay in time, the item becomes available again.

buying_an_item.title: How do I buy an item?
buying_an_item.summary: Buy an item at its asking price, or claim a free item.
buying_an_item.body:
You buy an item from its page with the **Buy Now** button.

1. Open the item.
2. Check the price and how you will get the item.
3. Press **Buy Now**.
4. If the item costs money, enter your card details and pay.

The order then appears in [My Orders](/marketplace/orders).

## Free items

For a free item, pressing **Buy Now** claims it. No money changes hands. Message the seller to agree when to collect it.

## Paying online

Online card payment only works if your community has switched it on and the seller has set up payments. If it is not available, you see a message when you try to buy. Message the seller to agree what to do instead.

When card payment is available, payments are handled by Stripe, a payment company. Card details are entered in Stripe's secure form.

> If a payment is not finished, the order is cancelled after a short time. You can then try again.

## If something goes wrong

Contact the seller first using **Message Seller**. If you cannot sort it out, contact your community administrator.

marketplace_orders.title: Following your orders and rating a seller
marketplace_orders.summary: Track what you bought, confirm when it arrives and leave a rating.
marketplace_orders.body:
Your purchases are on the **My Orders** page. Press **My Orders** under **Quick Links**, or go to [My Orders](/marketplace/orders).

Use the tabs **All**, **Active**, **Completed** and **Cancelled / Refunded** to sort your orders.

## Order statuses

- **Pending Payment**: payment has not finished yet.
- **Paid**: you have paid, or claimed a free item. The seller will now send or hand over the item.
- **Shipped**: the seller has sent the item. You may see a tracking number.
- **Delivered**: you have confirmed it arrived.
- **Completed**: the order is finished.
- **Cancelled** or **Refunded**: the order did not go ahead.

## Confirming delivery

When the item arrives, press **Confirm Delivery**, then confirm. This cannot be undone. The order becomes **Completed** after a waiting period.

## Rating the seller

Once an order is **Completed**:

1. Press **Leave Rating**.
2. Choose a **Rating**.
3. Add a comment if you like. You can tick **Submit anonymously**.
4. Press **Submit Rating**.

## For sellers

Orders for your items are on [My Sales](/marketplace/orders/sales). When you send an item, press **Mark Shipped**. Add a tracking number if you have one, then press **Confirm Shipped**.

reporting_a_listing.title: How do I report a listing?
reporting_a_listing.summary: Tell moderators about an item that is unsafe, illegal or breaks the rules.
reporting_a_listing.body:
If a listing looks unsafe, illegal, misleading or breaks your community's rules, please report it.

1. Open the listing.
2. Press **Report this listing**.
3. Under **Reason**, describe the problem.
4. Press **Submit Report**.

You see **Report submitted. Thank you.** and the report opens.

## Following your report

Go to [My reports and decisions](/marketplace/reports). It lists:

- Reports you have made, marked **Submitted by you**.
- Decisions about your own listings, marked **Affects your listing**.

Press **View report** to see the details. The status tells you where it has got to. For example: **Received**, **Under review**, **Action taken** or **No action**.

## Appealing a decision

If you disagree with a decision, you may be able to appeal.

1. Open the report.
2. Under **Appeal this decision**, explain why in **Appeal explanation**. Use at least 20 characters.
3. Press **Submit appeal**.

A different moderator reviews your appeal. The final decision appears on the same page.

> If an item puts someone in immediate danger, contact your local emergency services.

courses.title: Courses
courses.summary: Learn new skills from courses made by people in your community.

finding_courses.title: How do I find a course?
finding_courses.summary: Browse, search and filter the courses your community offers.
finding_courses.body:
You find courses on the **Courses** page. Open it from the **Community** menu, or go to [Courses](/courses).

## Searching and filtering

- Type in the **Search courses…** box to look for a topic.
- Use **All categories** to show one category only.
- Use **All levels** to choose **Beginner**, **Intermediate** or **Advanced**.
- Press **Load more** at the bottom to see more courses.

Each course card shows who made it and how many people have enrolled.

## Looking at a course

Press a course to open its page. There you can read:

- **About this course**, a description written by the course author.
- **Syllabus**, the list of sections and lessons.
- **Prerequisites**, any courses you need to finish first.
- **Reviews** from other learners.

The side panel shows the cost. It says **Free**, or a number of time credits. A time credit is one hour of time, the same currency you use in your wallet.

> Some courses are marked **Members only**. You see these only when you are signed in.

If you see the message **No courses found.**, your community has not published any courses yet. Check back later.

enrolling_in_a_course.title: How do I enrol in a course?
enrolling_in_a_course.summary: Join a course, pay any time-credit cost, and start learning.
enrolling_in_a_course.body:
You join a course by pressing **Enroll** on the course page.

1. Open [Courses](/courses) and choose a course.
2. Check the cost in the side panel.
3. Press **Enroll**.
4. You see the message **You're enrolled! Time to start learning.** and the first lesson opens.

## Paying for a course

Courses never cost money. A course is either free or costs time credits.

- The credits move from your wallet to the wallet of the person who made the course.
- You pay only once. If you leave and come back, you are not charged again.
- If you do not have enough credits, you see **You don't have enough time credits to enrol.**

## Courses you must finish first

Some courses list **Prerequisites**. These are other courses you must complete first. Until you do, the **Enroll** button stays switched off. The page shows **Complete the prerequisite courses to unlock enrolment.**

## Going back to a course

Once you are enrolled, the course page shows **Continue learning** instead. You can also find all your courses in [My learning](/courses/my-learning).

course_lessons_and_progress.title: Working through lessons
course_lessons_and_progress.summary: Open lessons, mark them complete and track your progress.
course_lessons_and_progress.body:
You work through a course one lesson at a time in the course player.

1. Open [My learning](/courses/my-learning).
2. Press **Continue learning** on the course.
3. Choose a lesson from the list on the left.
4. Read, watch or listen to the lesson.
5. Press **Mark as complete** when you have finished.

A tick appears next to finished lessons. The **Course progress** bar shows how far you have got.

## Types of lesson

A lesson can be text, a video, a PDF document, a page from another website, or a quiz. Some videos have a **Transcript**, which is a written version of what is said.

## Locked lessons

The course author can release lessons over time. A locked lesson shows a padlock and one of these messages:

- **This lesson isn't available yet.**
- **Available from** followed by a date.

Come back on that date and the lesson will open.

## Asking questions

Each lesson has a **Discussion** area. Type in the box and press **Post**. You can reply to others with **Reply**. You can delete your own comments with **Delete**. Only people enrolled in the course, and the people running it, can see the discussion.

## My learning

[My learning](/courses/my-learning) splits your courses into **In progress** and **Completed**.

course_quizzes.title: How do course quizzes work?
course_quizzes.summary: Answer quiz questions, see your score and try again if needed.
course_quizzes.body:
Some lessons are quizzes. You need to pass each quiz to finish the course.

1. Open the quiz lesson in the course player.
2. Answer each question.
3. Press **Submit answers**.

## Your result

Most questions are marked straight away. You see **Passed** or **Not passed yet**, and **Your score** as a percentage.

If you have not passed, change your answers and press **Submit answers** again.

## Answers checked by a person

Some quizzes include written answers. A computer cannot mark these. You see **Your answers were submitted for review.** The course author marks them later.

> You cannot mark a quiz lesson as complete until you have passed it. This also means you cannot get the course certificate until every quiz is passed.

course_certificate.title: Finishing a course and getting a certificate
course_certificate.summary: What happens when you complete every lesson, and how to print your certificate.
course_certificate.body:
When you complete every lesson in a course, you finish the course and receive a certificate.

When you finish, you see **You've completed this course.** You also get a notification and an email.

## Printing your certificate

1. Open [My learning](/courses/my-learning).
2. Find the course under **Completed**.
3. Press **Certificate**.
4. Your certificate opens in a new window, ready to print or save.

The certificate shows your name, the course, the date and a certificate ID.

> If nothing happens when you press **Certificate**, your browser may be blocking new windows. Allow pop-ups for this site and try again.

## Leaving a review

You can review any course you are enrolled in.

1. Open the course page.
2. Go to **Reviews**.
3. Choose a star rating under **Your rating**.
4. Add a comment in **Share your experience (optional)** if you like.
5. Press **Submit review**.

Your review appears straight away. If you review the same course again, your new review replaces the old one.

creating_a_course.title: How do I create my own course?
creating_a_course.summary: Build a course with sections and lessons, then publish it for others.
creating_a_course.body:
Many communities let members create courses. Some communities allow this only for chosen people, called instructors. If you are not allowed, you see an error when you save.

1. Open [Courses](/courses) and press **Create course**.
2. Fill in **Title**, **Short summary** and **Description**.
3. Choose a **Level**, a **Category** and a **Visibility**: **Public** or **Members only**.
4. Set a **Time-credit cost**. Leave it at zero for a free course.
5. Press **Save**.

## Adding lessons

After saving, the **Course builder** opens.

1. Press **Add section** and give it a **Section title**.
2. Press **Add lesson** inside the section.
3. Give it a **Lesson title** and choose a **Content type**.
4. Add the text, a video address, a PDF address or quiz questions.
5. Choose **Release timing** if you want the lesson to open later.
6. Press **Save lesson**.

For videos, please add a **Transcript**. People who cannot hear or watch the video rely on it.

## Publishing

Your course starts as a **Draft**. Press **Publish** to make it visible. In some communities an administrator checks courses first. Your course then shows **Pending review** until it is approved.

You can see all your courses in the [Instructor dashboard](/courses/instructor). It shows enrolments, completions, **Grading** and **Analytics** for each course.

podcasts.title: Podcasts
podcasts.summary: Listen to shows and audio stories made by members, or make your own.

listening_to_podcasts.title: How do I listen to a podcast?
listening_to_podcasts.summary: Find a show, play an episode and keep listening while you browse.
listening_to_podcasts.body:
You find podcasts on the **Podcasts** page. Open it from the **Community** menu, or go to [Podcasts](/podcasts).

1. Browse the shows, or type in **Search shows**.
2. Press a show to see its **Episodes**.
3. Press **Listen** on an episode.
4. Press **Play**.

## Using the player

- **Back 15s** and **Forward 30s** skip through the episode.
- The speed buttons play faster, up to 2x.
- If the episode has **Chapters**, press a chapter to jump to it.
- Some episodes have a **Transcript**. Press **Download transcript** to save it as a text file.

On a computer you can use the keyboard. Press Space to play or pause. Use the left and right arrow keys to skip, and the up and down arrow keys to change the volume.

## Listening while you browse

Once an episode is playing, a **Now playing** bar stays on screen as you move around the site. Press **Close player** to stop it.

## Carrying on later

If you stop part way, the episode page offers **Resume from** a time, or **Start over**. This is remembered on the device you used. It does not carry over to another phone or computer.

following_and_reporting_podcasts.title: Following shows and reporting episodes
following_and_reporting_podcasts.summary: Get told about new episodes, react to episodes and report a problem.
following_and_reporting_podcasts.body:
You can follow a show to hear about new episodes.

## Following a show

1. Open the show's page.
2. Press **Follow show**.
3. You see **Show followed.**

When a new episode is published, you get a notification. To stop, press **Unfollow show**.

Some public shows also have an **RSS feed** button. You can add this address to a podcast app on your phone.

## Reacting to an episode

If your community allows it, an episode page has a **React** button. Press it to show you liked the episode. Press it again to remove your reaction.

## Reporting an episode

If an episode is harmful, misleading or breaks someone's rights, please report it.

1. Open the episode page.
2. Press **Report**.
3. Choose a **Reason**: **Safety or harm**, **Spam or misleading content**, **Copyright or rights concern** or **Other**.
4. Add **Details for moderators** to explain the problem.
5. Press **Send report**.

You see **Report sent to moderators.** The community's moderators then review the episode.

creating_a_podcast.title: How do I start my own podcast show?
creating_a_podcast.summary: Create a show and add episodes in the Podcast Studio.
creating_a_podcast.body:
You make shows and episodes in the **Podcast Studio**. Go to [Podcast Studio](/podcasts/studio), or press **Create show** on the Podcasts page.

In most communities any member can create a show. If you are not allowed, the studio tells you.

## Creating a show

1. Under **Create show**, enter a **Show title**.
2. Choose a **Category** and add **Show artwork** if you have it.
3. Choose the **Visibility**. **Public** means anyone can listen. Some communities also offer **Members** and **Private**.
4. Add a **Summary** and **Description**.
5. Press **Create show**.

## Adding an episode

1. Under **Add episode**, choose the **Show**.
2. Enter an **Episode title**.
3. Upload your recording under **Hosted audio file**, or paste a web address in **Audio URL**.
4. Add a **Summary**, and a **Transcript** if you can. A transcript helps people who cannot hear the audio.
5. To release it later, use **Schedule publication**.
6. Press **Add episode**.

> Only upload audio you have the right to share, and get permission from anyone you record.

## Managing your shows

Your shows appear under **My shows**. Here you can edit, publish, archive or delete shows and episodes. In some communities a moderator checks new shows and episodes first. These show **Pending review** until approved.

**Listener stats** shows how many people listened to your episodes.

caring_community.title: Caring Community
caring_community.summary: Ask for everyday care, record kindness, support people you care for and raise a concern.

what_is_caring_community.title: What is the Caring Community?
what_is_caring_community.summary: A place in your community for everyday care, such as lifts, shopping and company.
what_is_caring_community.body:
The Caring Community is a part of the platform for everyday care between neighbours. Examples are a lift to an appointment, help with shopping, or some company for an afternoon.

Open the **Community** menu and choose **Caring Community**, or go to [Caring Community](/caring-community).

It works alongside timebanking. Time you give is counted in the same time credits as the rest of the platform. There is one balance, not a separate currency.

## What you can do from the hub

The hub groups its options:

- **Get help**: ask for practical support and see your support relationships.
- **Give help**: record a kindness, offer your time or log volunteering hours.
- **Your hours**: for example, gift some of your hours to someone else.
- **Safety & updates**: raise a safeguarding concern.

You only see options that your community has switched on.

## It is new

The hub says the Caring Community is brand new, and that some parts are early previews. It depends on neighbours volunteering their time. If your community also uses volunteering, press **I'd like to help** to see volunteering opportunities.

> The first time you visit, you may be asked **What brings you here today?** Your answer only changes which button is shown first. You can change it at any time.

requesting_care_help.title: How do I ask for help?
requesting_care_help.summary: Tell your community what practical help you need and how to contact you.
requesting_care_help.body:
You ask for help with the **Request Help** form.

1. On the [Caring Community](/caring-community) hub, press **I need some help** or **Request help**. You can also go straight to [Request Help](/caring-community/request-help).
2. Under **What kind of help do you need?**, describe what you need in your own words. You can use up to 500 characters.
3. Under **When do you need it?**, say when. For example, Tuesday afternoons, or as soon as possible.
4. Under **How should we contact you?**, choose **By phone**, **By message** or **Either is fine**.
5. Press **Request Help**.

You see **Request Received**.

## Speaking instead of typing

On some devices you can press **Tap to speak your request** and say what you need. The form is filled in from your recording. Check it carefully before you press **Request Help**. Nothing is sent until you press it.

## What happens next

Your request is saved for your community's care coordinators to review. You cannot see or change your request afterwards on this page.

> If you need help soon, or have not heard back, contact your community coordinator directly. If someone is in danger or needs urgent medical help, contact your local emergency services.

offering_a_favour.title: How do I record a favour?
offering_a_favour.summary: Record an act of kindness you did for someone. No time credits are involved.
offering_a_favour.body:
A favour is a small act of kindness you want to record. Examples are carrying shopping, giving a lift or sharing a meal. Favours do not earn or cost time credits.

1. On the [Caring Community](/caring-community) hub, press **Offer a Favour**. You can also go to [Offer a Favour](/caring-community/offer-favour).
2. Under **What did you do to help?**, describe what you did.
3. Choose a **Category** if you like, such as **Companionship** or **Transport**.
4. Under **When?**, choose the date. It starts as today.
5. Press **Record Favour**.

You see **Thank You!** Your community's coordinators can see the favours members record.

## Favours or time credits?

- Record a favour for an informal kindness you do not want credits for.
- To earn time credits for help you give, use timebanking or volunteering instead. On the hub, press **Offer time** or **Log hours**.

support_relationships.title: What are support relationships?
support_relationships.summary: See the regular support you give or receive, and pause or end it.
support_relationships.body:
A support relationship is a regular arrangement between a **Supporter**, who gives help, and a **Recipient**, who receives it. Your community's coordinators set these up. You cannot start one yourself.

To see yours, press **My Support Relationships** on the [Caring Community](/caring-community) hub, or go to [My Support Relationships](/caring-community/my-relationships).

## What each one shows

- The other person's name, and whether you are the **Supporter** or **Recipient**.
- How often you meet, such as **Weekly**, and the hours expected.
- The **Next check-in** date, or **Overdue** if it has passed.
- **Recent hours logged**, with whether each entry is **Approved**, **Pending** or **Declined**. Coordinators record these hours.

## Pausing, resuming or ending

- Press **Pause** to stop for a while. The status changes to **Paused**. Press **Resume** when you are ready to start again.
- Press **End relationship** to stop for good. This cannot be undone. Ended relationships no longer appear on this page.

> The other person is not told automatically when you pause or end a relationship. Please let them know yourself, or ask your coordinator to.

report_a_concern.title: How do I report a safeguarding concern?
report_a_concern.summary: Tell your community's safeguarding staff if you are worried someone is at risk of harm.
report_a_concern.body:
If you are worried that someone is being harmed, neglected or taken advantage of, you can report it.

> If someone is in immediate danger, contact your local emergency services first. Then make a report here.

1. On the [Caring Community](/caring-community) hub, press **Report a Concern**. You can also go to [Report a Safeguarding Concern](/caring-community/safeguarding/report).
2. Under **What kind of concern is this?**, choose the closest match.
3. Under **How urgent is this?**, choose from **Critical (immediate risk to a person)** to **Low (worth flagging)**.
4. Under **Describe your concern**, say what you saw or heard, when, and who was involved.
5. If you have a link to evidence, add it under **Evidence link (optional)**.
6. Press **Submit Report**.

You see **Report Submitted**.

## The optional boxes for people and organisations

**Person involved (optional)** and **Organisation involved (optional)** ask for a member or organisation number. If you do not know it, leave these empty. Give names in your description instead.

## Who sees your report

Your report is seen by the people who handle safeguarding in your community, such as coordinators and administrators. They can see that you made the report. The person you report about cannot see your report.

Choose **Critical** only when a person is at immediate risk. In an emergency, always contact your local emergency services as well.

my_safeguarding_reports.title: Checking on a concern you reported
my_safeguarding_reports.summary: See the status of the safeguarding reports you have made.
my_safeguarding_reports.body:
You can see the safeguarding reports you have made on the **My Safeguarding Reports** page.

Go to [My Safeguarding Reports](/caring-community/safeguarding/my-reports). You can also press **View my reports** straight after you submit a report.

Each report shows how urgent it is, the type of concern, the start of your description and the date you sent it.

## What the statuses mean

- **Submitted**: your report has been received.
- **Triaged**: staff have looked at it and decided how to handle it.
- **Under investigation**: staff are looking into it.
- **Resolved**: staff have finished dealing with it.
- **Dismissed**: staff decided no further action was needed.

You may also see **Escalated**. This means the report has been raised for more urgent attention.

> You are not sent a notification when the status changes. Come back to this page to check. This page does not show what action was taken. If you are still worried, contact your community coordinator directly.

linking_a_care_receiver.title: How do I link to someone I care for?
linking_a_care_receiver.summary: Ask to be recorded as the caregiver of a member you already look after.
linking_a_care_receiver.body:
If you already look after a member informally, you can ask to be linked as their caregiver. This gives you some caregiver tools, such as asking for help on their behalf.

1. On the [Caring Community](/caring-community) hub, press **Become a caregiver**. You can also go to [Link a Care Receiver](/caring-community/caregiver/link).
2. Under **Find member**, type at least 2 letters of their name and choose them.
3. Choose the **Relationship**: **Family member**, **Friend**, **Neighbour** or **Professional carer**.
4. Enter the date under **Care started**.
5. Add **Notes** if you like. The person you care for can see these.
6. Press **Link a care receiver**.

## The checks before the link is active

A link does not start straight away. It goes through two checks:

1. The person you care for is told and must agree. The status shows **Waiting for the care recipient**.
2. Your community's staff then review it for safeguarding. The status shows **Waiting for staff safeguarding review**.

When both are done, the status shows **Active** and you are both told. If the link is refused, it shows **Not approved**.

> If a request is declined or withdrawn, you must wait 7 days before asking again.

caregiver_dashboard.title: Using the Caregiver Dashboard
caregiver_dashboard.summary: See the people you care for, their care schedule, and answer caregiver requests about you.
caregiver_dashboard.body:
The **Caregiver Dashboard** brings together the people you care for. Go to [Caregiver Dashboard](/caring-community/caregiver).

## If you are a caregiver

**People I care for** lists the people you are linked to. For each active link you can:

- Press **View care schedule** to see **Upcoming care** and **Recent care**.
- Press **Request help on their behalf** to open the Request Help form for them.

To add someone, press **Link a care receiver**.

If you log a lot of volunteering hours in one week, the dashboard shows a reminder to rest. Looking after yourself matters too.

## If someone asks to be your caregiver

You get a notification when a member asks to be linked as your caregiver. The link in the notification opens this dashboard. Under **Caregiver requests about me**:

- Press **Confirm relationship** only if you know this person and agree.
- Press **Reject request** if you do not agree.

No caregiver tools are given to the other person until you agree and staff have checked the request.

> If you did not expect a request, or feel pressured, press **Reject request**. Then talk to your community coordinator.

gifting_hours.title: How do I gift hours to someone?
gifting_hours.summary: Give some of your time credits to family, friends or anyone who needs them.
gifting_hours.body:
You can give some of your banked hours to another member of your community. These are the same time credits as in your wallet.

1. On the [Caring Community](/caring-community) hub, press **Gift Hours**. You can also go to [Gift Your Hours](/caring-community/hour-gift).
2. On the **Send** tab, find the person under **Who would you like to gift hours to?**. Type at least 2 letters of their name.
3. Enter **How many hours?**. You can see how many hours you have available.
4. Add a personal message if you like.
5. Press **Gift Hours**.
6. Check the details and press **Yes, gift hours**.

The hours leave your wallet straight away. They reach the other person when they accept.

> The other person may not get a notification about your gift. Let them know you have sent it, and ask them to open **Gift Hours** and check their **Inbox**.

## Receiving a gift

Open the **Inbox** tab. Press **Accept** to add the hours to your wallet. Press **Decline** to send them back.

## Changing your mind

On the **Sent** tab, a gift waiting to be accepted shows **Awaiting acceptance**. Press **Withdraw gift** to cancel it. The hours come back to you.

premium_offers.title: Donations and partner venues
premium_offers.summary: Support your community with a donation, and use your membership pass at local venues.

donating_to_your_community.title: How do I donate to my community?
donating_to_your_community.summary: Give a one-off gift or set up a regular donation by card.
donating_to_your_community.body:
If your community accepts donations, you can give money by card to support it. Open the **Community** menu and choose **Donate**, or go to [Donate](/premium).

## Giving once

1. Press **Make a one-off donation**.
2. Enter the **Amount** and choose the **Currency** and **Fund**.
3. Add a message, or choose **Donate anonymously**, if you like.
4. Press **Continue to Payment**, then enter your card details and pay.

When it works, you see **Thank You!** and can view your receipt.

## Giving regularly

Your community may offer support levels for regular giving.

1. Choose **Monthly** or **Yearly** at the top of the page.
2. Pick a support level and press **Donate regularly**.
3. You are taken to a secure payment page run by Stripe, a payment company. Enter your card details there.
4. When you return, you see **You are all set!**

If you see **Still processing…**, your payment is going through. Press **Check status** after a moment.

> Donations are gifts to your community. Giving regularly does not unlock extra features on the platform, and it does not change how other members see you or match with you.

Money donations are separate from time credits. You earn time credits by giving your time.

managing_regular_donation.title: Changing or cancelling a regular donation
managing_regular_donation.summary: See your regular donation, update your card or stop giving.
managing_regular_donation.body:
You manage a regular donation on the **My Support** page. Go to [My Support](/premium/manage).

The page shows your support level, whether you pay **Billed monthly** or **Billed yearly**, and the **Next billing** date.

## Updating your card or payment details

Press **Manage in Stripe**. This opens Stripe's billing page, where you can update your card.

## Cancelling

1. Press **Cancel regular donation**.
2. Confirm that you want to cancel.

You see **Regular donation will end at the period end**. You are not charged again. Your donation stays active until the end of the period you have already paid for.

## If a payment fails

The page shows a message asking you to update your card by a date. Press **Manage in Stripe** to update it.

## Changing your support level

Before choosing a new level, cancel your current regular donation. This makes sure you are not paying for two at once. Then press **Change support level** and choose the new level.

If you see **No active regular donation**, you are not giving regularly at the moment. Press **View support levels** to start.

partner_venue_pass.title: Using your membership pass at partner venues
partner_venue_pass.summary: Find local venues that welcome members and show your pass when you visit.
partner_venue_pass.body:
Partner venues are local places, such as cafés, shops and community spaces, that welcome members of your community.

## Finding venues

Open the **Community** menu and choose **Partner venues**, or go to [Partner venues](/venues). Each venue shows what it offers members, its address and a link to its website.

## Your membership pass

1. Press **My pass** on the venues page, or go to [My membership pass](/venues/pass). You can also press **My venue pass** in your wallet.
2. A QR code appears on screen.
3. When you visit a partner venue, show this code to the staff.
4. The staff scan it and confirm your visit.

Your visits are listed under **Recent visits**. A visit can be recorded once per venue per day.

> The platform only records your visit. It does not take any payment or apply any discount. Any offer is given by the venue itself.

## Keeping your pass safe

If you think someone has copied your code, press **Replace my code**. Your old code then stops working.

## If you are venue staff

If your community has added you as staff at a venue, scan a member's pass with your phone camera. Sign in if asked, then press **Record visit**.
